title: Project Evaluation Consultant
body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23684**  
Position Title: **Project Evaluation Consultant (Type B)**  
Duty Station City: **Port Vila**  
Duty Station Country: **Vanuatu**  
Contract Type: **Consultant B**  
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**  
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **2 months**  
Closing date: **03 November 2026**

**Context:**

Since 2015, more than 30 per cent of Ni-Vanuatu citizens have experienced temporary or protracted displacement due to disasters. Vanuatu's approximately 300,000 people (Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics, 2020) spread across 83 islands are exposed to cyclones, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, ashfalls, earthquakes, mudslides, flooding and drought. As the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events increases due to climate change, disasters pose a primary threat to Vanuatu's national security and human development.

Tropical Cyclones (TC) Judy and Kevin (both of Category 4 intensity) made landfall over Vanuatu on 1 and 3 March 2023. TC Judy and Kevin affected an estimated 24,657 households (123,288 people) with 90 per cent of houses in Shefa and Tafea provinces destroyed or severely damaged. The cumulative impact of compounding events such as previous cyclones (TC Harold), high La Nina rainfall and COVID-19, has had a devastating impact on basic living conditions, access to basic services, livelihoods, and coping capacities. While traditional resilience in Vanuatu is strong, emergency preparedness needs strengthening at all levels - national, provincial, area council and community – particularly in light of intensifying climate change impacts in the Pacific.

In response, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is implementing a project to support the Vanuatu National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) in strengthening the capacity of national and provincial government institutions, Community Disaster and Climate Change Committees (CDCCCs), Area Councils, faith-based organizations, and community leaders — particularly women leaders — to develop and maintain safe and dignified evacuation arrangements during emergencies.

This builds on the existing work being undertaken by the Displacement and Evacuation Centre Management (DECM) Cluster which brings together key partners to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities. It will strengthen and extend the work of the DECM Cluster to provincial and community level, moving towards improved localization of emergency response measures in Vanuatu.

Specifically, the Sef Ples Blong Yumi Phase 2 project funded by the Government of Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), implemented by the National Disaster Management Office, Vanuatu in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration, supports the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness, coordination, and evacuation centre management across multiple hazards. The project focuses on strengthening the DECM Cluster’s coordination capacity, updating and rolling out the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and Evacuation Toolbox / Training Materials, improving information management systems, and supporting preparedness at national, provincial, and Area Council levels.

**The Objective of the project is:**

To contribute to the protection and resilience of people at risk of displacement in Vanuatu by supporting the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness and evacuation procedures.

The project will update and finalize the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and developing the Evacuations Toolbox / Training Materials for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to strengthen:

1. National, provincial and area council-level coordination of evacuations.
2. Capacity of communities, CDCCCs, faith-based groups to manage and lead their own community-based evacuations in ways that both draws on traditional knowledge about evacuations and increases protections for vulnerable groups, especially women, children, older people and people with disability.

The Outcomes and Outputs of this project are the following:

Outcome 1: Government, faith-based groups and communities have enhanced capacity to coordinate, develop, maintain and monitor safe, dignified evacuation accommodation in emergencies.

Output 1.1: Improved information management at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in sudden-onset emergencies.

Output 1.2: Improved coordination at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in emergencies.

Output 1.3: Updated National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines and Evacuations Toolbox for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

Output 1.4: Roll out of Evacuations Toolbox training for national trainers, Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Disaster Risk Reduction - Humanitarian

Project code: CC0083

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**The Final Evaluation Report shall include the following sections:**

- Executive Summary
- Introduction, objectives, methodology, and limitations
- Findings (relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability and cross-cutting issues)
- Discussions of outcomes and results
- Lessons learned and good practices (success factors and/or those which challenged performance)
- Conclusions
- Recommendations
- Annexes (i.e. TOR, Data Sources, Evaluation Matrix, etc.)
- Further details of the deliverables are:
    
    **Other general tasks to be undertaken as part of this assignment will include**
- Providing advice and input to project direction and methods.
- Reporting to and keeping up good communication with National Programme Officer and Project Manager.
- Attendance at project meetings online or in person.
- Meetings, where requested, with IOM Chief of Mission, IOM Project Staff, or Government of Vanuatu representatives.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Performance should be assessed according to the tangible and measurable deliverables of the work assignment as stated in Section 7 above.
- Payment instalments to be made upon the satisfactory completion of each of the deliverables and approval by the project manager.
- Performance will be assessed against the outputs as provided above.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- The evaluator should preferably have a master's degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 2 years of relevant professional experience.
- Or the evaluator should have a bachelors degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 4 years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in carrying out similar evaluation assignments for projects related to humanitarian preparedness, response, recovery, disaster resilience, climate change, evacuation center management, or displacement and evacuation center management coordination.
- Demonstrated capacity to coordinate with and secure key informants (including government actors, community networks, other key stakeholders, and community participants) is required.
- Minimum 4 years of experience working with research, policy development, analysis, monitoring and evaluation, and program evaluation preferably in the field of climate change, disaster risk reduction, emergency response, and / or environment.
- Understanding of Vanuatu displacement, emergency response, evacuation centres, and climate change context are an advantage
- Experience of working in the Pacific region is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Good communication and coordination skills.
- Computer skills required (MS Word and basic MS Excel) for reporting.
- Strong facilitation, mentoring, and stakeholder coordination skills.

**Languages**

- For this consultancy, Fluency in Bislama and English language is required. Working knowledge of French is an advantage.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

One trip to Port Vila will be required as part of this ToR:  
Trip 1: Approximately 10 days (estimated early - December 2026 or early January 2027) – this travel is required to coordinate evaluation activities, attend meetings, and conduct key informant interviews. Exact dates of the trip to be coordinated between IOM Project Management Team and the selected evaluator(s).  
If budget allows a second trip can be considered in mid or late January 2027.  
IOM will cover costs relating to round trip airfares, accommodation, and a consultant / evaluator daily subsistence allowance. Travel and health insurance will not be covered by IOM and is the responsibility of the consultant / selected evaluator(s).

title: Website Redesign and Development Consultancy

title: Helios+ Center Assistant
body:
**BACKGROUND:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children. Since 2019, IRC Hellas implements an alternative care project for unaccompanied children and will now pilot this project to Greek born children and adults.

**SCOPE OF WORK:** Helios+ - Comprehensive Actions for the integration of Third Country Nationals in the Labor Market - (MIS 6016874) is a portfolio of regional Integration Projects, dedicated to fostering the integration of third-country nationals into Greece's labor market and society. Designed by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) with the support of the Government of Greece (GoG), co-financed by the European Union under the Regional Programs (RP) for 2021–2027 and aligns fully with Greece's National Strategy for Integration. HELIOS+ is committed to empowering Beneficiaries of International and Temporary Protection residing in Greece by providing them with the tools and resources needed to achieve socio-economic independence and actively participate in the Greek community, while promoting self-reliance and inclusion through a comprehensive set of services tailored to the needs of the target group.

In the Attica Region, International Rescue Committee Hellas participates as a partner of IOM Greece, together with Solidarity Now, in the consortium led by Caritas Hellas.

The IRC supports access to job counseling and job matching, life skills, education and psychosocial support – directly and in collaboration with partners. The IRC is recruiting a HELIOS+ Center assistant for the reception and registration of beneficiaries, providing first-level information, and guiding beneficiaries to the specialized services of the center. The HELIOS+ Center assistant will also be responsible for preparing the necessary documents for their registration, monitoring the security of the center, and ensuring the smooth operation of the center’s overall spaces and equipment.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Welcome and receive beneficiaries and visitors to the Center warmly and friendly**;**
- Provide information about the Center and its services to the beneficiaries of the subproject, as required**;**
- Provide administrative support to ensure the smooth daily operation of the Center**;**
- Manage the Center’s calendar and scheduling of sessions, appointments, etc., in coordination with the Center’s Manager**;**
- Manage the Center’s correspondence and communications (phone/email/mail)**;**
- Update and maintain a contact list**;**
- Effectively maintain filing systems, both electronic and paper-based**;**
- Collect and organize the data required for each beneficiary;
- Monitor the Center’s spaces and their security, maintain cleanliness and order, aim to ensure smooth and efficient operation, in close cooperation with the Center’s Manager;
- Other related duties as assigned by the subproject Coordinator;
- Participate in regular team meetings and external meetings as requested;

**REQUIREMENTS:**

- BA/BS Degree in Pedagogical Studies, Administrative Studies, and/or other related fields;
- At least three (3) years of experience in a corresponding position of responsibility, preferably in the field of humanitarian organizations;
- Excellent knowledge of Greek and English, spoken and written (level C1/C2).
- Computer skills, in particular word processing, excel spreadsheets and internet services;
- Excellent interpersonal, team and communication skills;
- Ability to organize and prioritize workload using initiative;
- Ability to work under pressure;

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS:**

- Experience in customer service.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks.
- Intercultural awareness and flexibility.
- Ability to work on own initiative and at the same time as part of a multicultural and interdisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of French, or Arabic, or Farsi, or Pashto, or Urdu is an advantage.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

Working hours: 9:00-17:00

Travel and other requirements: Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs within Athens

**This position is expected to end on May 30, 2027.**

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: £1,300 - £1,590/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Short Description**

IOM, UN Migration Agency in Geneva, Switzerland is looking for a consultant who will consolidate and harmonize existing guidance on return, readmission and reintegration including the readmission manual and the technical guidance on return and reintegration, into a single integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR).

**Description**

**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

To support rights-based migration governance, the consultant will consolidate and harmonize existing guidance on return, readmission and reintegration including the readmission manual and the technical guidance on return and reintegration, into a single integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR). The final document will be primarily targeted at government practitioners and authorities responsible for the development, implementation and management of return, readmission and reintegration processes, while also serving other relevant stakeholders. The guidance will aim to clarify the applicable standards and frameworks for rights-based RRR management and provide concrete operational recommendations to help practitioners establish or strengthen RRR systems including through effective inter-State cooperation.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Within the Department of Mobility Pathways and Inclusion, under the overall supervision of the Head of the Border Management, Returns and Readmission Division, and under technical management of the Head of the Return and Reintegration team and the Head of the Immigration, Visa, and Readmission Unit, and in close coordination with Cooperation on Migration and Partnerships to Achieve Sustainable Solutions (COMPASS).

**Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

Produce a coherent and comprehensive integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR) based on the consolidation and harmonization of the existing draft of the Technical Guidance on Return and Reintegration, developed by IOM’s Regional Office in Vienna, and the draft Readmission Manual, developed by the Immigration, Visa, and Readmission Unit in IOM’s Headquarters. More precisely the consultant will:

1. Identify overlaps and complementarities, and propose the appropriate structure and lay out of a coherent document for optimal user experience.
2. Consult appropriate teams and partners as needed.
3. Integrate the concepts and guidance from both documents into a single coherent narrative.
4. Ensure the final document is primarily targeted at government practitioners and authorities responsible for the development, implementation and management of return, readmission and reintegration processes, while also serving other relevant stakeholders.
5. Prepare dissemination material for external use.

**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. **Context**

The Office of Legal Affairs provides legal advice to the Director General, the Deputy Directors General, the regional offices, the country offices, and other departments and offices of the Organization. The Office provides support to ensure that the activities and operations of the Organization are carried out in accordance with the legal framework governing IOM, including the IOM Constitution, decisions of the governing bodies of IOM, the Unified Staff Regulations and Rules, the Financial Regulations and Rules, IOM instructions and international law.

The General and Administrative Law Division is responsible for:

- Advising on misconduct cases and the management of disciplinary processes, including the imposition of disciplinary and non-disciplinary measures.
- Reviewing the legality of contested decisions in formal Requests for Review by staff members.
- Representing the Organization in internal justice processes, including the Joint Appeals Review Board and the International Labour Organization Administrative Tribunal.
- Reviewing investigation reports and other findings of the Office of Internal Oversight in relation to IOM personnel.
- Reviewing policies related to management and human resources, including revisions to the Unified Staff Regulations and Rules, instructions and other issuances.

title: 23246 Programme Officer (Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)) (P)
body:
Launched in August 2021 with funding from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the Better Regional Migration Management (BRMM) Programme is IOM’s flagship labour migration programme in the East and Horn of Africa (EHOA). The programme supports efforts to strengthen labour migration governance, promote fair and ethical recruitment, enhance the protection of migrant workers and their families, and expand access to safe, orderly and regular labour migration pathways. Building on earlier phases, the current BRMM FY26–27 framework focuses on operationalising skills-to-employment, skills mobility and ethical recruitment systems for safe labour migration in the EHOA. It prioritises scalable and evidence-based interventions that improve access to decent work, strengthen national and regional labour migration systems, and contribute to reducing reliance on irregular migration routes. The programme will be implemented in four priority countries—Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia and Uganda—while continuing to support regional cooperation through the Regional Ministerial Forum on Migration (RMFM), Regional Economic Communities and relevant national institutions. It places particular emphasis on vulnerable groups, including youth, women, returnees, refugees and migrant workers, and supports interventions related to labour market information systems, public employment services, skills development and recognition, bilateral labour migration agreements, ethical recruitment, migrant protection, reintegration and engagement with countries of destination, including the Gulf States. A strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning approach, together with communication and visibility efforts, will support adaptive management, donor accountability and the documentation of results and lessons learned.

Under the overall supervision of the EHOA Regional Director and direct supervision of the Regional Program Management Officer, Labour Mobility and Human Development, the Programme Officer (Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)) will be responsible for the implementation of the M&E aspects of the BRMM program in line with the expectations of the donors.

**Responsibilities**

1. Lead and be responsible for the overall Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) function of the BRMM project, including the development, updating and implementation of the project M&E plan, results framework, data collection tools, quality assurance mechanisms and monitoring procedures.
2. Provide regular technical M&E support to implementing missions, including guidance on data collection, activity monitoring, results tracking, reporting requirements, data quality and the accurate reflection of M&E plans in mission-level action plans.
3. Lead the collection, consolidation, analysis and use of BRMM project monitoring data to track progress against agreed indicators, inform programme decisions, identify implementation gaps and ensure that programme-related datasets are accurate and up to date.
4. Prepare BRMM biannual and annual reports by compiling, verifying and analysing inputs from implementing missions, ensuring that reported results are evidence-based, consistent with donor requirements and aligned with the project results framework.
5. Review and provide technical guidance on activity concept notes, mission activity reports and related workplans, ensuring that M&E requirements, indicators, targets, verification methods and follow-up actions are clearly and accurately reflected.
6. Undertake monitoring visits to implementing missions, as required, to assess progress, verify reported results, support corrective actions and provide hands-on guidance on the implementation of BRMM M&E processes.
7. Design, coordinate and conduct surveys, outcome monitoring exercises, impact assessments and other learning or evidence-generation activities when required by programme needs or requested by the donor.
8. Support adaptive management, learning and accountability by tracking risks, assumptions, lessons learned and emerging results; ensuring responsible data management; and providing evidence-based recommendations to improve BRMM implementation, reporting and donor accountability.
9. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Statistics, Economics, Public Policy, Migration Studies, International Relations, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.
- Specific training or certification in Monitoring and Evaluation, Results-Based Management, data analysis, research methods, or impact assessment would be an advantage.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in leading Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) functions for complex projects, including the development and implementation of M&E plans, results frameworks, indicators, data collection tools, quality assurance mechanisms and monitoring procedures;
- Demonstrated experience in Project Cycle Management (PCM), Results-Based Management (RBM), monitoring data collection, consolidation, analysis and use of evidence to inform programme implementation, reporting and adaptive management;
- Experience in providing technical M&E support to implementing missions or field teams, including guidance on activity monitoring, results tracking, data quality, reporting requirements and the integration of M&E plans into action plans;
- Experience in preparing high-quality donor reports, including biannual and annual reports, by compiling, verifying and analysing inputs from implementing partners or missions and ensuring alignment with results frameworks and donor requirements;
- Experience in reviewing activity concept notes, activity reports, workplans and related documentation to ensure that M&E requirements, indicators, targets, verification methods, risks, assumptions and follow-up actions are clearly reflected;
- Experience in conducting monitoring visits, surveys, outcome monitoring exercises, evaluations, impact assessments or other evidence-generation activities to assess progress, verify results and support programme learning;
- Experience in maintaining programme datasets, ensuring responsible data management and producing evidence-based recommendations to strengthen implementation, accountability, learning and donor reporting; and,
- Experience in labour migration, migrant protection, ethical recruitment, bilateral labour migration agreements, skills mobility or related migration governance programming would be an advantage.

**Skills**

- Strong communication and coordination skills, including the ability to present M&E findings clearly, provide practical guidance to implementing missions, and communicate evidence-based recommendations to programme teams, management and donors;
- Strong analytical skills, including the ability to collect, verify, consolidate and interpret quantitative and qualitative data for reporting, learning and decision-making;
- Excellent report-writing skills, including the ability to prepare evidence-based donor, biannual and annual reports aligned with results frameworks and reporting requirements;
- Ability to provide technical M&E guidance and capacity support to implementing missions, including on activity monitoring, data quality, reporting and the integration of M&E requirements into concept notes and action plans; and,
- Ability to conduct monitoring visits, surveys, outcome monitoring, impact assessments and learning exercises to support adaptive management and donor accountability.

title: 22969 Protection Officer (P)
body:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Liberia is working in close collaboration with the Government of Liberia, United Nations agencies, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), and international partners to address the complex migration, humanitarian, and development challenges exacerbated by decades of conflict, displacement, and instability.

Under the supervision of the Chief of Mission and in close cooperation with relevant departments at Headquarters (HQs) and Regional Office (RO), the Protection Officer will be responsible and accountable for managing, coordinating and overseeing the Country Office’s (CO) Protection Programme activities and strategies, including child protection, counter-trafficking, violence against women and girls, men and boys, Disability Inclusion, assistance to vulnerable migrants, and overall specialized protection programming in the CO.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical advice to CO management and programme teams on the design and delivery of protection programming and support in leading the protection Mainstreaming across relevant programme activities to strengthen safe programming and the protection capacity of staff and partners.
2. Contribute to the design of, implement, and monitor migrant protection interventions in line with IOM protection standards, protection principles, and rights-based approaches, providing inputs on strategic options to the COM and positioning IOM's response to the evolving needs of migrants.
3. Provide technical guidance on protection case management, vulnerability screening, protection assessments, and assistance to migrants in vulnerable situations to raise the quality and consistency of case handling across the CO.
4. Develop and maintenance referral pathways and coordination mechanisms with governmental, UN, Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs) and civil society protection actors to widen vulnerable migrants’ access to specialised services.
5. Facilitate protection risk analysis and integrate mitigation measures throughout programme design and implementation to embed protection mainstreaming across operational activities and reduce risks to affected populations.
6. Review and monitor compliance with IOM protection standards, data protection principles, Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) commitments and other relevant institutional policies and frameworks to identify gaps and recommend corrective action.
7. Conduct CO protection assessments and analyses of protection risks, service gaps, and emerging trends affecting migrants and vulnerable populations to generate evidence that informs CO strategy and programme adjustments.
8. Manage the implementation of protection projects by monitoring activities, expenditures and deliverables, and bringing issues to the attention of the Resources Management Officer (RMO) and the COM with proposed solutions for timely corrective action.
9. Provide operational management, guidance, supervision , and mentorship to relevant programme staff, advising on programmatic strategy and implementation, resource allocation and operational challenges, and deliver trainings that builds team performance and capacity.
10. Participate in technical coordination meetings, protection working groups and inter-agency forums to promote IOM’s technical positions that strengthen partnerships and the coherence of the collective protection response.
11. Prepare technical inputs for donor reports, concept notes and project documentation and share programme information with relevant stakeholders for donor confidence and transparency.
12. Identify programme priorities in coordination with the relevant units at the CO, ROs and HQ, as well as with government counterparts and other relevant partner organisations, and develop project proposals and activities built on a solid results framework, responding to emerging trends and priorities, donor interests and requirements and IOM’s institutional strategies, policies and guidelines.
13. Prepare quality programme reports and submit in a timely manner, in coordination with relevant units in the CO and in line with IOM, donors’ and relevant stakeholders’ requirements.
14. Develop and maintain data collection and analysis mechanisms for IOM’s ongoing or new programmes and share relevant information with partners to strengthen evidence-based decision-making.
15. Assess programme progress against strategic objectives and programme benchmarks, and provide advice on improvements and corrections, and manage the development of a common Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) framework with regular reporting requirements and impact evaluation strategies in coordination with CO’s Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL) team.
16. Conduct regular field visits to manage, coordinate, and support the implementation of protection programmes, identifying operational challenges and enabling timely adjustments in delivery quality.

**Education**

- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in migrant protection, child protection, counter-trafficking, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), protection mainstreaming or related protection fields;
- Experience conducting protection assessments and vulnerability analyses;
- Experience working with migrants in vulnerable situations and managing complex protection cases;
- Experience coordinating with protection actors and referral systems;
- Experience developing and delivering protection-related capacity-building activities;
- Experience within IOM, UN, NGOs or humanitarian protection programming considered a strong asset;
- Experience in programme development;
- Experience in liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities as well as with national and international institutions; and,
- Experience in organising consultations, workshops and seminars with high-level stakeholders.

**Skills**

- Strong knowledge of migrant protection principles, protection mainstreaming and specialised protection programming;
- Strong knowledge of IOM and inter-agency protection standards, operational procedures and guidelines;
- Knowledge of protection case management, referral systems and protection-sensitive approaches;
- Knowledge of IOM protection frameworks, data protection principles and PSEAH standards.

title: Legal Migration Expert
body:
## I. Background

Seefar implements Raising Awareness of the Dangers of Irregular Migration II (RADIM II) across four governorates in Federal Iraq including Baghdad, Basra, Dhi Qar, and Al-Muthanna. RADIM II aims to reduce irregular migration by strengthening awareness at individual and community level, providing targeted psychosocial and practical support to at-risk youth, and connecting individuals to viable local and overseas alternatives.

A core element of RADIM II is ensuring that young people who are considering irregular migration and have the potential to migrate legally, are supported to do so.

## II. Objective of the Position

Seefar plans to appoint a Legal Migration Advisor to deliver specialist advice to programme participants with strong prospects of successfully obtaining work or study visas abroad. The assignment is part-time and deliverables based. It is expected to run from October 2026 to March 2027, with the potential to convert to a full time position during that period. The Advisor must be based in Federal Iraq.

## III. Key Responsibilities

1. Support the development of a legal advisory training curriculum. This will include conducting 10-12 interviews with potential candidates and two focus group discussions to help us understand how best to position the service.
2. Build rapport with 15-30 candidates who have been screened for legal mobility. You will collaborate with the MEL Analyst to select the candidates, then set up tailored engagement plans which seek to remove the barriers to mobility for each one and identify a high-prospect pathway to migration.
3. Across 1:1 advisory sessions and ad-hoc follow up, provide the candidates support with their applications and help them to succeed.
4. Complete monitoring forms as requested and provide regular feedback to the team, so we can continually improve the service.
5. Conduct a short exercise to test the willingness of candidates to pay for the service in the long term, as part of the service’ plan for longer term sustainability. (Note: this is only a test and candidates will not be charged.)
6. Take part in training and coaching as required by your supervisor.

The Legal Migration Expert shall provide guidance across some or all the following pathways, and may propose additional legal routes based on demand and their expertise:

- Legal labour migration and overseas employment
- Investment-based migration routes
- Student visa applications and study-abroad pathways
- Scholarships and funded study opportunities
- Family reunion.
- Other legal migration or mobility pathways relevant to youth

Sessions will be delivered online and in person.

## IV. Remuneration

You will be paid GBP 900 (approx. USD1,200) per month for a maximum of five months, with an expectation that you work approximately 20 hours per week. In each month, you’ll be expected to handle a caseload of 8 -10 ongoing and new candidates. Conversion to a full time contract depends on performance and external funding.

title: East Africa Programme Officer
body:
**Job Title:** East Africa Programme Officer  
**Reports To:** Africa Regional Manager  
**Status:** Full-Time  
**Direct Reports:** Interns/volunteers, where relevant. (At present, this role doesn’t have direct reports)  
**Contract duration:** Two years (with the possibility of extension depending on funding)  
**Compensation:** ETB 2,093,000–2,898,000 annually  
**Location:** This post is based in Addis Abba, Ethiopia. Please note that IDC is unable to support relocation and the postholder needs to have the ability to work in Ethiopia.

**Background**

International Detention Coalition (IDC) is a unique global network, of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, that coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention.

**Role Purpose**

We are seeking a highly organized and motivated individual with a solid background in advocacy on migration and human rights. The ideal candidate will coordinate projects, initiatives and events efficiently, contribute to strategic advocacy efforts and support the development of the capacity of IDC members. Strong communications, organizational, planning, and stakeholder engagement skills are essential.

**Role Summary**

The Africa Programme Officer will play a key role in supporting IDC’s mission in the region by combining strong organizational and coordination skills with a solid understanding of advocacy on migration and human rights. Working closely with the Africa Regional Manager and other team members, the Programme Officer will contribute to the design and implementation of regional programs, events, initiatives and advocacy strategies. The role involves providing operational, administrative, research, and communications support, as well as helping to strengthen networks with members, partners, decision makers and other key stakeholders across the Africa region and specifically in Eastern Africa. The Programme Officer should be available to travel within the region as needed.

**Role Responsibilities**

**Project implementation, admin support and support to IDC members and partners**

- Contribute to the implementation of national and regional projects and events by providing technical, administrative, and logistical support to the Africa Regional Programme and in collaboration with relevant IDC staff and members
- Support the overall implementation of IDC’s mission and strategic priorities in the Africa region (with a priority focus on Easter Africa) through a balance of operational efficiency and advocacy engagement.
- Support IDC’s members in the region and support in network building.
- Maintain a high level of organization in managing project timelines, deliverables, and follow-ups in coordination with the Africa Regional Manager and other relevant team members.

**Advocacy and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Contribute to drafting and disseminating advocacy materials, briefing notes, and strategic communications tailored to diverse audiences across the Africa region.
- Maintain regular contact with IDC members and partners to identify policy gaps, advocacy opportunities, and spaces for support, partnership and coordinated action.
- Assist in the planning and facilitation of stakeholder consultations, trainings, and regional events that promote rights-based alternatives, pathways and regional dialogue.

**Communication**

- Disseminate and share resources among members and other stakeholders through different platforms.
- Contribute to monitoring media platforms and keep track of reports and updates on relevant developments in the region.

**Internal Systems, Monitoring, Fundraising, and Institutional Support**

- Actively contribute to IDC’s fundraising efforts by providing background research, identifying potential funders, coordinating inputs, and play an active role in the drafting of proposals aligned with regional priorities
- Ensure accurate and timely monitoring and reporting of programmatic activities, supporting internal evaluation processes and donor accountability in line with IDC’s MEL systems.

The ability to take initiative and to work remotely and autonomously, to manage competing deadlines, prioritise workload appropriately and work in a flexible manner. title: 22867 Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) (P)
body:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) – the United Nations (UN) migration agency – in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) implements a broad, integrated programme supporting crisis‑affected populations and national institutions in a context of protracted conflict, large‑scale displacement, and limited access to essential services. The programme combines humanitarian assistance, stabilization, durable solutions, peacebuilding, migration governance, and border management interventions across multiple provinces, targeting Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, host communities, ex‑combatants, vulnerable households, and government counterparts. Core activities include community‑based planning, rehabilitation of key infrastructure, livelihood and reintegration support, social cohesion initiatives, displacement tracking, protection services, and capacity building for national and local authorities. Through these efforts, IOM aims to strengthen resilience, restore basic services, enhance local governance, and advance sustainable solutions for displacement‑affected communities.

Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director of the Regional Office (RO) for East Horn and Southern Africa (EHSA) and direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and in close coordination with the Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS) and relevant Divisions/Departments/Units at Headquarters, the Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) will provide strategic leadership and oversight across the Country Office’s (CO) programme portfolio. This includes guiding programme development and implementation, leading strategic planning processes, strengthening donor and government engagement, ensuring coherence with One UN frameworks, overseeing programme support functions, and maintaining high‑level coordination with national authorities, UN agencies, partners, and stakeholders. The Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) will also ensure integrated planning, quality assurance, knowledge management, and effective representation of IOM in inter‑agency fora, while supporting the COM in advancing the CO’s priorities and institutional objectives.

**Responsibilities**

1. Oversee the overall development, implementation, and monitoring of programme activities under areas of responsibility, including oversight of IOM’s cluster participation and ONE UN obligations. Identify potential and existing obstacles to programme delivery through continuous monitoring of new programme areas that reflect changes in host country and donor priorities.
2. Develop the CO’s programme overview, including all (or thematically relevant) programmes implemented by the CO, and schedule the major activities for the COM.
3. Lead the development of country strategic plans, which are in line with IOM’s global & regional strategies, the Country National Peace & Development Strategy, and the One UN Programme.
4. Lead the development of the CO’s donor and partner outreach strategies, taking into account priorities in DRC, Humanitarian Response and Recovery, and IOM’s regional and global strategic priorities and objectives; implement the strategies in close coordination with the COM and CO’s relevant units.
5. Develop and maintain Government working relationships with the ministries and international agencies involved in migration-related issues in DRC, and maintain regular liaison with key government officials and interlocutors. Serve as overall Focal Point for Humanitarian Response and Recovery.
6. In coordination with the COM and CO’s relevant units, establish liaison and maintain continuous dialogue with relevant stakeholders (i.e., national governmental authorities, donors, UN Agencies, national and international Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), national and international institutions, Private sector) aiming at coordinating and facilitating the implementation of ongoing activities and promoting new activities and fundraising for new projects; identify synergies with IOM’s programmes and make recommendations on donor/partner engagement.
7. Lead the Programme Support Unit and supervise the Unit’s staff providing project development, public information, reporting, donor relations, government liaison and information management functions for the CO.
8. Ensure an integrated approach to CO’s programming, with required support functions such as project development, reporting, donor relations, public information and information management are provided to programme units in a timely manner.
9. Provide overall guidance to Programme Managers on project development, public information, donor relations, government liaison and information management; ensure consistency and coherence of project/ programme activities in accordance with the CO’s strategies and in coordination with the RO and relevant departments/units at HQ.
10. Provide guidance and support to the Heads of Sub-Offices on the CO’s priorities, policies and strategies.
11. Identify programme strategic priorities in relevant service areas and areas of interest in line with IOM mandate and expertise, aiming to further expand the CO’s partnership basis and the scope of activities.
12. Act as Focal Point for government liaison and oversee the CO’s correspondence and reporting to the government authorities; ensure that the CO’s interests are accurately communicated and promote IOM’s visibility.
13. Represent the CO in inter-agency fora, including but not limited to the Programme Management Team (PMT) and One UN, and One Programme.
14. Lead knowledge management and capacity building activities in the CO.
15. Prepare policy guidance notes, documentation and briefs for COM and senior management.
16. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Business or Public Administration, International Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Extensive experience in programme formulation, implementation and evaluation;
- Demonstrated supervisory experience in staff management;
- Proven record of establishing and maintaining good working relationships with governmental and diplomatic authorities, national, regional and international institutions, as well as civil society actors;
- Previous work experience in a rapid transition or post-conflict area;
- Demonstrated experience in liaising with governmental authorities, international agencies (i.e., UN), and civil society organizations;
- Experience in project development, implementation, and reporting, including financial and budgetary aspects; and,
- Familiarity with inter-agency programme regulations of the UN and other donors.

**Skills**

- In-depth knowledge of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Sound judgment, ability to analyze information and make decisions rapidly to resolve operational problems;
- Efficiency, flexibility, high level of professionalism and ability to adhere to strict deadlines;
- Strong leadership, management, and coordination ability;
- Sound communication and interpersonal skills;
- Ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and backgrounds;
- Familiarity with IOM’s Migrant Management Operational Systems Application (MiMOSA) and Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) systems;
- Knowledge of the IOM project management cycle; and,
- Knowledge of IOM’s administrative and financial management.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: Logistics coordinator (F/M) - Syria
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Syria**

Since December 2024, about 1.8 million refugees and 2 million internally displaced people have returned to their areas of origin (UNHCR, 1 October 2026, indicative), and many others remain displaced. Many return to areas where roads, public services, and health facilities are damaged or only partially functional. Humanitarian needs remain high, while access, administrative procedures and security conditions can change quickly from one area to another.

Médecins du Monde (MdM) works in Syria to protect vulnerable people's access to essential health care, including returnees and displaced communities. Our programs are run from the coordination office in Damascus, with teams and partners in several governorates.

MdM is currently operating in Aleppo and Idlib governorates, supporting three health facilities. Since 2026, program activities have been extended to Rural Damascus and Daraa governorates, where MdM will support two health centers.

**About the role**

You will provide strategic and technical leadership to the logistics team, support program planning and proposal development, manage logistics risks and ensures compliance with MdM France procedures, donor requirements, and applicable Syrian regulations.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the general coordinator, you define, plan and implement all supply and logistics activities, while ensuring budget compliance and respect of MdM’s protocols and procedures. You lead and manage the logistics team.

More specifically, your main responsibilities are:

- Define, plan and budget logistical needs for the mission and monitor logistical activities
- Define, implement and adapt procurement plan and procedures
- Manage contracts related to logistics and supply activities
- Recruit and manage the logistics team, set objectives, define training needs, ensure skills management
- Ensure monitoring and reporting on logistical activities, adapt indicators when needed
- Supervise and manage the transportation of goods and people
- Supervise the installation and maintenance of office and accommodation areas
- Define and monitor IT and communication resources
- Ensure that the archiving system for logistics documents is respected
- Participate in the definition, implementation and monitoring of the safety and security standards
- Provide logistics guidance, training, advising and technical support to all field teams

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the logistics advisor at HQ, the program coordinators and the health managers, the support coordinators, the MEAL team and the security focal point, among others.

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following : logistics, supply chain management, procurement, business administration or a related field.
- Have at least 5 years of relevant professional experience, including experience in a coordination or management role in a humanitarian or international NGO setting.
- Have experience managing local and international supply chains, preferably including medicines and health commodities.
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently, Arabic is highly appreciated

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in premises management, infrastructure, energy systems and rehabilitation or renovation works.
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in complex, restrictive and volatile operational environments.
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of October.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 392 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Damascus, Syria
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: Consultancy on MMC Development of a Standard DAC Estimation Tool - SUIDAC Project
body:
Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement affected people and communities. DRC works during displacement at all stages: In the acute crisis, in displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, or upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence.

MMC is a knowledge centre engaged in data collection, research, analysis, and policy and programming on mixed migration. MMC has regional hubs hosted in Africa, Asia, Europe and Latin America, with a global team headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and based in several countries worldwide. MMC is a leading source for independent and high-quality data, research, analysis and expertise on mixed migration. MMC aims to increase understanding of mixed migration, to positively impact global and regional migration policies, to inform evidence-based protection responses for people on the move and to stimulate forward thinking in public and policy debates on mixed migration. MMC’s overarching focus is on human rights and protection for all people on the move. The MMC is part of and governed by the Danish Refugee Council. For more information on MMC visit our website ([http://www.mixedmigration.org/](http://www.mixedmigration.org/)).

## Purpose and Objective of the consultancy

The overall purpose of the consultancy is to design, test, validate and document a standardized DAC Estimation Tool that can be implemented by cities/municipalities across the nine SUIDAC target cities. The consultancy directly contributes to Activity 1.1 and Activity 1.3 of the SUIDAC project which require the review of existing approaches to estimating DAC populations and the development of a standardized and replicable estimation methodology for use by city authorities. The consultant will work closely with MMC, city authorities, Technical Implementing Partners (TIPs) and other relevant stakeholders to develop a practical, rigorous and scalable methodology that enables cities to estimate DAC population size and distribution.

## Deliverables

The Consultant will contribute to the following task:

**Phase**

**Expected deliverables**

**Indicative description tasks**

**Maximum expected timeframe**

**Task 1**

**Literature and Methodological review and Assessment of existing city data sources**

- Conduct a review of global, regional and country specific methodologies used to estimate Displacement Affected Communities (DAC).
- Analyze and assess the feasibility of integrating available data sources for DACs with municipal, national and humanitarian data sets.
- Identify methodologies suitable for low-data urban environments and produce recommendations for the SUIDAC context.

**13th November -31st December, 2026**

**Task 2**

**Development of the DAC Estimation Tool**

- Design a standardized and replicable estimation framework suitable for all SUIDAC cities
- Design user-friendly and city-specific methodology note to be shared with city officials.
- Develop a practical implementation model that municipalities can apply without advanced statistical expertise.

**13th November – 31st December, 2026**

**Task 3**

**Determination of DACs per City**

- Test out the methodology for city-level DAC population estimations and develop estimates. This will be dependent on municipality fieldwork/data provisions in order to develop an estimate.
- Establish methodological groundings for confidence intervals, margin of errors and contextual estimation notes for the SUIDAC cities.

**1st December, 2026 – 19th February, 2027**

**Task 4**

**Validation and stakeholder consultation**

- Present the findings of the DAC estimates and the methodology note to MMC and facilitate consultation and validation workshops.
- Incorporate feedback and update methodology note
- Document lessons learned and methodological refinements.

**22nd February -5th March, 2027**

**Task 5**

**Finalisation and Capacity Building Package**

- Finalize the methodology and user guidance materials including the training guide and practical implementation guidance for municipalities.
- Prepare technical documentation outlining assumptions, limitations and recommended applications for MMC and city authorities.

**8th March – 31st March 2027**

The Consultant will provide the documentation***by email on a Word, PDF document and link format.***

## Duration, timeline, and payment

The consultancy will run for five (5) months, from Mid November 2026 to March 2027.

Payment Schedule is:

1. 20% of the total costs upon signing of the contract
2. 50% upon completion of tasks 1-3 in the deliverables above
3. 30% upon satisfactory completion of the tasks, methodology note, DAC estimation per city and capacity building package.
    
    ## Proposed Composition of Team

- Principle DAC estimation consultant

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

### Essential:

- A degree and post-graduate degree in Statistics, International Affairs, Political science ,Demography, Economics, Data Science, Geography, Migration Studies, Urban Planning, Public Policy, BA in Political Science; MA in International Affairs and Development; a related area of study.
- A minimum of 5 years broad and deep experience with conducting applied research on urban forced displacement populations in fragile contexts
- Ddemonstrable experience in developing population estimation or demographic methodologies.
- A strong and proven background (e.g. through prior publications), knowledge and understanding of urban displacement regionally and globally.
- Proven experience in statistical modelling and estimation techniques using administrative, survey, census and geospatial data sets.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to work independently, meet deadlines, and manage multiple tasks.
- Excellent analytical and reporting skills, particularly for donor audiences.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Prior experience with MMC is a plus.

## Technical supervision

The selected consultant will work under the supervision of:

- ***Head of MMC Eastern and Southern Africa,***
- ***MMC Data and Research Manager***

## Location and support

Most coordination with MMC will take place virtually through weekly calls and weekly update emails.

The Consultant will provide a computer and any other required electronic equipment needed for the assignment.

## Travel

No travel will be required for this assignment.

## **About us**

The Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation (MF) is an international rights-based, survivor-centred organisation, dedicated to ending sexual violence as a weapon of war globally. The Mukwege Foundation supports survivors’ demands for a world where sexual violence as a weapon of war is no longer tolerated, and bears consequences for individual perpetrators and states. We work for a future where survivors receive the holistic care and compensation they need to rebuild their lives. We create opportunities for survivors to speak out and be heard, and where they can organise to create change, influence policies, and demand justice and accountability.

## **Background**

At the Mukwege Foundation, everything we do is guided by a five-year strategy (2024–2028) and a mission that matters: supporting survivors of conflict-related sexual violence and changing the global response to the use of sexual violence as a weapon of war. Communications are how that mission reaches people, helping them to understand and engage with the change we are working to achieve.

As our Communications Intern/Volunteer, you’ll help organise our communications assets, from powerful photos and videos to the archives and systems behind them. Your work will make our stories easier to share and use for years to come, so the voices of survivors keep reaching the people who need to hear them.

## **What you’ll gain**

This is your chance to get real, hands-on experience in a dynamic international non-profit organisation.
