title: Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert - CDR
body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/200**
- **Position Title**: Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert - CDR
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 3 months (without exceeding 16 working days per month).
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 14 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 21 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JFJvvMi0X1CMbBMR4IhA-Zv5eASVx6wv/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JFJvvMi0X1CMbBMR4IhA-Zv5eASVx6wv/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

The successful implementation of CDR’s digital transformation requires the establishment of a clear governance and implementation foundation before major technology investments and platform deployments can proceed. This includes defining ownership and decision-making arrangements, validating the target structure and functions of the Information Technology Department, establishing an enterprise architecture and data governance framework, and ensuring that core business processes are appropriately re-baselined to reflect the future operating model. It also requires a clear understanding of CDR’s existing technology, systems, data, infrastructure, and security environment, together with a structured approach to prioritizing investments and addressing critical gaps.

Therefore, a set of foundational measures have been identified to be undertaken during Stage 1 of the Digital Transformation Roadmap. These measures are intended to establish the rules, governance arrangements, technical and organizational architecture, inventories, and implementation baseline required to guide subsequent phases of digital transformation. They include the establishment of programme governance arrangements, validation of the target IT Department structure and enterprise architecture, definition of data governance principles, risk-based re-baselining of core processes, and preparation of the inventories, procurement strategy, terms of reference, and multi-year budgets required to move from planning to implementation. Immediate actions have also been identified to strengthen CDR’s existing backup, recovery, and cybersecurity arrangements using available tools and resources, alongside urgent remediation measures that need to be initiated.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert to support CDR in delivering Stage 1 of the Digital Transformation Program. The Expert will establish the programme governance arrangements and implementation baseline, validate the target IT Department structure and enterprise architecture, define the foundations for data governance, and validate the priority use cases of the document management system and the shared workflow system. The Expert will also prepare the key inventories, procurement strategy, terms of reference, and multi-year budget requirements needed to enable subsequent digital investments and implementation.

Through this assignment, the Expert will support CDR in moving from the recommendations of the Functional and Business Process Review to a structured and implementable digital transformation programme, ensuring that the institutional, governance, process, technical, procurement, and financial foundations are in place before major digital platforms and systems proceed to implementation.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Program Governance and Mobilization**

- Within two weeks of mobilization, agree with CDR the process scope, the technical changes, the available working days and the resources required for this assignment, and prepare a work plan that schedules the remaining work with its owners, dependencies and costs.
- Support CDR in establishing the governance bodies of the Digital Transformation Program, comprising the ICT Steering Committee, the Data Governance Committee and the Technical Review Committee, and prepare their terms of reference, their decision rights and the responsibility matrix that assigns each decision to a named body. The terms of reference of the ICT Steering Committee cover its decisions, escalation arrangements, meeting frequency and progress reporting. Support CDR management in formally designating the interim ICT Transformation Lead and the business and technical owners of critical systems and services.
- Support the establishment of the Digital Transformation Program Office function, comprising the integrated roadmap, the dependency register, the risk register, the benefits plan, the procurement plan, the architecture decision log and the reporting calendar, and hand the instruments over in working order.
- Assist in validation of the target structure and staffing of the Information Technology Department against the functions the program requires, the existing staff and their workload, and coordinate the resulting job descriptions with the human resources workstream so that a single set of descriptions is produced. Prepare the responsibility matrix of the Department, identify staffing and skills gaps, and recommend interim assignments, training and specialist support. Formal appointments and organizational decisions remain with CDR.

**Workstream 2. Architecture and Data Governance**

- Develop and validate the enterprise architecture and the digital building blocks against the baseline covering the business, data, application, integration, technology and governance domains. Produce an updated high-level application and integration diagram, confirm the roles of JDE, the document management system, ArcGIS and the planned systems, and record the compatibility issues, dependencies and decisions required before procurement.
- Support in establishing the standing coordination arrangement with the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform and, where relevant, with the national digital acceleration program, with a designated focal point, a defined agenda covering hosting, interoperability, digital identity and electronic signature, and a reporting line to the ICT Steering Committee.
- Prepare the initial data governance principles, covering named business data owners, authoritative systems, shared project and contract identifiers, minimum metadata, access and classification, data quality, retention and controlled sharing. Submit the principles, with the validated enterprise architecture, to the ICT Steering Committee for endorsement.

**Workstream 3. Process Re-baselining and Technical Readiness**

- With the business service owners, review the process maps to identify the common requirements for the document management system and the shared workflow system. Validate representative use cases, bottlenecks, document types and control needs to the level required for the terms of reference. Validate the approval thresholds and segregation of duties for these use cases, and record unresolved decisions and required authorizations. Produce a prioritized catalogue of business flows for later implementation. Full process redesign and configuration follow in later stages.
- Prepare the system, application, asset and workload inventories, including hardware, software licenses, contracts and support arrangements, and record the baseline performance indicators, or the method for collecting them where data are not yet available, against which the benefits of the program are later measured. The inventories record quantities, condition, capacity, hosted workloads, owners, dependencies, support status and renewal dates. They also assess workstation upgrade readiness and the priority server, storage, backup, scanner and power-protection needs. The workload inventory of the hosts designated for retirement, prepared by the firm contracted for the server refresh, is incorporated rather than repeated.

**Workstream 4. Procurement and Funding Readiness**

- Prepare the phased procurement strategy. The strategy specifies the document management system and the shared workflow system during this assignment, establishes and accepts the platform in a later stage, and configures the priority business flows in successive releases. Identify the packages, dependencies, lead times and owners, and define separate deliverables and acceptance gates for the platform foundation and for each business-flow release.
- Prepare the technical specifications, quantities and supplier pricing schedule for the justified priority hardware, infrastructure and services. Compare reuse, support renewal, repair and replacement, and include capacity, compatibility, migration, warranty, support response, acceptance testing and staff handover requirements.
- Reconcile the installed software and its use with entitlements and contracts. Verify the current vendor lifecycle and upgrade terms for operating systems, productivity tools, server and database licenses, electronic mail, endpoint protection, backup, firewalls and core applications. Identify renewals, unused entitlements and license gaps, and prepare a costed renewal and upgrade schedule.
- Prepare the terms of reference for the document management system and the shared workflow system, assessing the modernization of the existing SharePoint environment against its replacement. Define document capture, metadata, search, versioning, retention, permissions and audit trails; reusable forms, routing, approvals, notifications and monitoring; configurable roles, approval rules and audit controls; integration with JDE and identity services; and migration, hosting, licensing, training and support. Specify the platform acceptance tests and the later releases of priority business flows. The requirements preserve CDR data ownership, editable documentation, interoperability, portability and exit rights, with brand-neutral specifications where feasible.
- Prepare the indicative multi-year budget for the three-year horizon of the roadmap, separating implementation costs from recurring costs, and covering operations, maintenance, staffing, training, security reviews, licensing, hosting, support, hardware refresh, integration maintenance and contingency, and confirm the institutional and budget owner of each system before procurement.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 16 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 16 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed by the 31st of January 2027.

Any continuation of the services beyond this period, including the second phase of support described in the Background, is subject to a separate contract or a formal amendment of this contract. Continuation depends on satisfactory performance under this contract, the continued requirement for the services and the availability of funds.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Digital Transformation, Information Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Public Administration or a related field. Specialized focus on enterprise architecture, information systems, digital transformation, data governance, cybersecurity, or ICT management is highly preferred.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) designing, managing, or implementing digital transformation and information management programmes, including ICT governance, enterprise architecture, systems integration, data governance, and business-process digitization; and (ii) providing strategic and technical advice on ICT infrastructure, cybersecurity, information systems, technology procurement, and digital transformation planning, preferably in public-sector or institutional environments.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

title: External Consultant (Category B) – Endline Evaluation for Displaced Afghans Regional Programme
body:
Position Title: **External Consultant (Category B) for the Endline Evaluation of the Project "Support to Displaced Afghans in Pakistan, Iran, Central Asia, and Afghanistan (EU/DG INTPA-funded)"**  
Duty Station: **Kabul, Afghanistan**  
Expected Start Date of Deployment: **01 November 2026**  
Deployment Duration: **5 months**

**Background:**

The Islamic Republic of Afghanistan and its neighboring countries Pakistan, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and Tajikistan – together constitute one of the world’s most complex and protracted displacement contexts. Sustained conflict, economic collapse, climate shocks, and large-scale cross-border return have combined to produce acute and overlapping humanitarian, protection, and reintegration needs that extend well beyond Afghanistan’s borders. Since 2021, the region has absorbed sustained, high-volume returns of undocumented and documented Afghans from Iran and Pakistan, while smaller but significant caseloads of Afghans on the move and at risk of displacement remain present in Tajikistan and the wider Central Asia sub-region. It is this regional character of the crisis – and not Afghanistan alone – that defines the programme under evaluation.

IOM’s programme, funded by the European Union through DG INTPA and implemented across three Top-Up phases over a total duration of 63 months (with a revised end date of 31 March 2027), was designed accordingly as a two-outcome, four-country regional response. Outcome 1 covers the regional response in Pakistan, Iran, and Tajikistan; Outcome 2 covers the Afghanistan-based response. Programme design, resource allocation, and results reporting are structured around this regional architecture, and the evaluation must be resourced and scoped to reflect it in full not as an Afghanistan evaluation with regional context, but as a four-country regional evaluation with an Afghanistan component.

**Roles and Responsibilities of the Consultant:**

- Develop and finalize the evaluation matrix, methodology, and country-specific data collection tools, fit for purpose in each of the four programme countries.
- Design and apply an appropriate sampling methodology for each country and for the regional comparison.
- Lead the training and supervision of any locally engaged field data collectors in each country, ensuring adherence to the agreed protocol and methodology.
- Coordinate and technically oversee the two-phase field data collection exercise across all four countries, including locally engaged data collectors and other approved field support, and ensure consistent application of the evaluation methodology, ethical standards and data-quality requirements.
- Assure data quality through supervision and database review.
- Submit the Inception Report, Draft Report, and Final Report using agreed IOM templates.
- Present findings to the Evaluation Reference Group and other key internal and external stakeholders.

**Qualifications and Experience of the Consultant:**  
The assignment shall be undertaken by an individual Consultant with demonstrated technical expertise and experience appropriate to the scale, complexity and regional nature of the evaluation. Applicants will be assessed against the following minimum and desirable requirements:

**Minimum Requirements:**

- An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or higher) in evaluation, research, public policy, migration studies, humanitarian assistance, international development, public health, social sciences or another field directly relevant to the assignment.
- A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in evaluation, including the design and implementation of complex evaluations for UN agencies, EU-funded programmes, multilateral organizations or comparable international development/humanitarian actors.
- Demonstrated experience leading or undertaking complex multi-country or regional evaluations, preferably involving displacement, migration, humanitarian response, durable solutions or related programming.
- Demonstrated expertise in mixed-methods evaluation, including quantitative and qualitative research design, sampling, development of data collection instruments, data analysis, triangulation and evidence synthesis.
- Demonstrated thematic experience relevant to the programme, including forced displacement/migration, protection, livelihoods/economic resilience and/or area-based approaches.
- Demonstrated experience integrating relevant cross-cutting considerations, including gender equality, protection, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations and PSEAH, into evaluation design, data collection, analysis and reporting.
- Demonstrated experience producing high-quality evaluation reports and presenting complex findings and recommendations to institutional stakeholders and donors.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

**Desirable Requirements:**

- Previous evaluation or research experience in Afghanistan and/or the wider regional context covered by the evaluation, including Pakistan, the Islamic Republic of Iran and Tajikistan/Central Asia.
- Demonstrated knowledge of the UN system, IOM's mandate and/or EU/DG INTPA-funded programming.
- Knowledge of one of more relevant regional languages, including Dari, Pashto, Farci, or Urdu is an asset.

title: Quality Assurance Analyst, METAL
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

We aim to make our programs a model for the highest global standards and to cultivate power and lasting change not just for our clients but for all people affected by humanitarian crises. To achieve that vision, the IRC’s Technical Excellence (TE) group, located within the Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department, provides technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff and shares what we learn to influence policy and practice.

IRC’s Technical Excellence team is comprised of seven teams which have deep expertise in their respective fields: Education, Economic Wellbeing, Governance, Health, Violence Prevention and Response, MEAL, and Grants & Operations.

**Measurement, Evaluation, Technology, Accountability, and Learning at the IRC**

The METAL Unit is responsible for supporting CRRD to have a culture of strong data and evidence use through stewardship of the Data & Performance Ecosystem, and for coordinating successful piloting and uptake of innovative technology solutions. The METAL Unit provides specialized support across four pillars to strengthen program effectiveness, improve decision-making, and enhance organizational learning.

**This is a hybrid position open to candidates based in New York, US, Kenya and UK. Other Limited IRC Locations may also be considered. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.**

**Job Overview**

The METAL Quality Assurance Analyst will be part of the METAL team which is responsible for delivering products that support day-to-day implementation of CRRD Programs as well as the collection, management, visualization of KPIs relevant to higher-level decision-making.

The QA Analyst is a team member responsible for developing, testing, implementing, and supporting CRRD’s data toolkits, for which the tech stack includes CommCare, Microsoft Power BI, and Microsoft SQL server Azure-based data warehouse.

The Data Toolkits are essential for CRRD’s data collection, management and analysis so it is critical for the success of the team that the QA Analyst have strong skills related to testing data transformation and visualization.

Working in partnership with staff at various levels and locations, the QA Analyst will perform a key role in testing, assuring quality, and improving Data Toolkits with a successful rollout. Should demonstrate a solid focus on responsive application design and an understanding of the diverse subject areas involved in developing user-centric and impactful applications.

Position key attributes are multi-tasking, detail orientation, fast learning, and self-organizing. The candidate is required to not only test the technology products, but also to identify, create, and implement complex use case scenarios; take a lead in efforts to find requirement/specification gaps and work very closely with business teams/analysts to seek answers. Find a balance between keeping high-quality standards without overly exerting on the release timeline. Build a good working relationship between development and product management teams. Be able to turn around testing and regression testing within timelines without compromising on quality.

This role reports to the Product Manager. Program Technology. The QA Analyst will work closely with METAL Developers. They will have a technical line to the Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and maintain regular contact with the QA team to ensure that METAL is following the best practices of the wider organization.

**Major Responsibilities**

Primary responsibilities include but are not limited to:

- Translate functional requirements and specifications into detailed test plans, encompassing functional, system, integration, performance, regression, and user acceptance testing. The individual in this role will implement Agile Software Testing with Scrum principles.
- Work with the project management team closely to ensure that testing processes are implemented and followed by all core team members.
- Maintain high quality of applications developed in CommCare/Microsoft PowerApps meet user needs.
- Perform in-depth data testing of PowerBI dashboards and underlying data pipelines, including data verification across systems, data migration testing, data validation testing, and A/B testing, to ensure the accuracy, integrity, and quality of visualized data and the overall user experience.
- Review products to match design specifications, with an eye to user experience issues such as fonts, colors, and screen size breakpoints with responsive design.
- Verify multiplatform capabilities, cross-browser testing (Chrome, IE, Firefox, Edge, Safari), and mobile testing (iPad, iPhone, android phone, tablet) for build products.
- Ensure all testing is planned, implemented, and delivered per the latest industry standards, and to our quality expectations while meeting ambitious timelines.
- Fully own the assigned project’s testing stream – Perform requirement analysis and proactively find requirements gaps; discover and write test cases in Jira; create and maintain regression test case documents; sign off for release; do release smoke test.
- Identify application defects, seek resolution, process gaps, and make recommendations to improve the functionality and usability of the application.
- Call for the test case review meetings with the core team.
- Clearly communicate the testing timeline for each testing phase. Help the team set a realistic release timeline such that a testing effort is not overlooked or overly simplified.
- Ensure all identified risks from testing are raised and mitigated appropriately

**Key Working Relationships**

- Position Reports to: Product Manager, Program Technology
- Direct Reports: None
- Management in Partnership: Senior Manager, Quality Assurance

**Key Internal Relationships:**

- METAL Technology Development Lead
- METAL Developers

**Desired Experience and Skills**

- 3+ years of data application testing experience, with proven experience managing and executing the full testing lifecycle, including UAT testing support
- 2+ years of Quality Assurance experience testing data processes and products: ETL pipelines, dashboards/reports, etc
- 2+ years of working with CommCare or similar ODK based platforms or any low-code application as an application developer or quality analyst is highly desirable.
- Some Performance and Load Testing experience with open-source tools
- 1 year of automation experience
- Solid ability to lead a project by him/herself from all quality assurance, and quality control aspects.
- Experienced testing in low to no-code environments and processes such as mobile data collection and/or case management tools such as CommCare, Ona, Kobo or Microsoft PowerApps, PowerBI dashboards and Azure.
- Understanding and experience with T-SQL, Azure SQL Server, Data Factory, SSIS/other ETL tools, data modeling and data warehouse.
- Experience testing multilingual platforms along with multicurrency verification preferred.
- Manual functional testing, system testing, along with some automation, and performance testing
- Have great collaboration with all teams involved in the project with self-directed.
- Meticulous in maintaining excellent organization and prioritization skills
- Experience using Jira for bug and test management.
- Experience with full software development process with Agile methodology
- Experience with any open-source performance/stress testing tool e.g., JMeter
- Possess excellent oral and written communication skills
- Self-motivated and a problem solver
- Fast and independent learner
- Work with distributed teams
- Intercultural competence

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree or experience in computer science or information systems.
- CSQA, CSTE, or any certification software testing/ quality assurance

title: Regional Business Development Manager- SWANA
body:
**About The Role**

**Team Purpose**  
Institutional funding is key for operationalizing Oxfam’s mandate globally and in the region. Institutional sources (including multilateral and bilateral agencies and donors) typically have decentralised operations, budgets and decision-making structures throughout the world. To engage effectively with these organisations Oxfam has an established global architecture that mirrors its key institutional relationships, builds stronger partnerships and delivers greater impact and influence at country, regional and global levels. This operational architecture also enables Oxfam to more readily purse multi-country / regional opportunities that are offered by institutional donors to address transnational issues such as migration, climate change, natural disasters and conflicts. Humanitarian crises which often cross-national borders also require standing capacity at regional levels to most effectively mobilise resources.

**Job Purpose**  
The Regional Business Development Manager will lead on new business development in support of all countries in their region; creating, identifying and accessing new funding opportunities; maintaining a consistent standard of donor relationship and high-quality proposal development across variable country contexts; and will actively seek to grow income for the confederation through multi-country funding opportunities and consortium partnerships.

The Regional Business Development Manager will also support the Regional Director in providing strategic leadership on resource mobilisation across all countries in the region. They will be responsible for developing and implementing the regions resource mobilisation strategies; supporting the Regional Director in building partnerships with regional donors and civil society stakeholders; identifying new funding opportunities; addressing key financial and reputational risks; and ensuring that there are strategies in place to maintain adequate skills and capacity, staffing and income within the portfolio of countries in the region.

The post holder will be expected to work across the confederation of Oxfam affiliates and the Oxfam International Secretariat in achieving the regional funding strategy and be the primary link for accessing technical fundraising assistance and support from the confederations fundraising architecture.

title: Protection Analyst—Research and Advocacy
body:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

***Context:***

The consultancy will support the Government of the Republic of Armenia in advancing integrated border management reforms and strengthening interagency cooperation in line with the draft Integrated Border Management (IBM) Strategy and related Action Plan priorities, as well as European Integrated Border Management principles.

The consultancy will focus on enhancing cooperation among the National Security Service Border Guard Troops, State Revenue Committee, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Migration and Citizenship Service, and other relevant border management stakeholders in line with European Integrated Border Management (EIBM) principles and international best practices.

The assignment will support the institutionalization of interagency cooperation and operational coordination mechanisms, the application of integrated risk analysis approaches based on the Common Integrated Risk Analysis Model (CIRAM), the development of standard operating procedures and joint operational practices, and the strengthening of information-sharing and coordinated response capacities.

The consultant will develop an interagency training package with primary focus on interagency cooperation, operational coordination, information exchange, and risk analysis, while integrating relevant aspects of border security, human rights, integrity, and emerging border management challenges.

Through a combination of assessment, curriculum development, practical exercises, simulation-based learning, and capacity-building activities, participating institutions will strengthen their ability to conduct coordinated border management operations, apply common risk analysis methodologies, enhance information exchange, and respond effectively to border security challenges in accordance with EU IBM standards.

  
***Background of the activity:***

The Project is implemented in Armenia to further strengthen the capacities of the national authorities to tackle cross-border organized crime and independent border management capacities. The primary national partners benefiting from its outcomes are the National Security Service of the Republic of Armenia (NSS) and its Border Guard Troops (BGT). The Project will build on the results achieved in recent years and will further advance the alignment of the border guard training/ educational system and standards with European and international best practices, enhance capacity to autonomously manage borders through enhanced secondary inspection as well as capacity to detect and counter irregular travellers, including terrorists and serious criminals through setting up Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) data.

- Produce a Training Needs and Capacity Assessment Report with recommendations.

- Interagency cooperation and coordination;
- Risk analysis and CIRAM methodology;
- Information exchange and operational coordination;
- Joint operational planning and decision-making.

- Trainer guides;
- Participant handbook;
- Presentations;
- Practical exercises;
- Case studies;

- operational coordination;
- crisis management;

- document fraud;
- human rights considerations.

title: Regional Programme Coordinator (MENA)
body:
The Red Cross Red Crescent Movement is the world's largest humanitarian organization, and we are looking for a **Regional Programme Coordinator** in the **International Department, Middle East and North Africa (MENA) Region**. As **Regional Programme Coordinator**, you will be responsible for coordinating and managing multi-country regional programmes, ensuring high-quality implementation, monitoring, reporting, learning, and stakeholder engagement across the MENA region. The role focuses particularly on the implementation and expansion of the **Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) Programme** and the **Pathways to Protection (P2P) Programme**, while supporting strategic programme development, partner capacity strengthening, and donor compliance.

Danish Red Cross has been present in the Middle East and North Africa region since 2002, working closely with Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Yemen, the occupied Palestinian territory, Egypt, and other countries in the region. DRC supports programmes in health, migration, disaster preparedness and response, National Society Development, and community resilience. The current regional portfolio includes the NCD Programme, supported by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and the World Diabetes Foundation, and the Pathways to Protection Programme, funded by the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and implemented through a consortium approach focused on migration and protection across North Africa.

**Your main tasks include:**

- Coordinate and oversee the implementation of regional programmes, ensuring activities, budgets, and deliverables are delivered on time and to a high standard.
- Lead programme planning, reporting, monitoring, learning, and donor compliance processes across multiple countries and partners.
- Support National Societies and country teams through technical guidance, capacity strengthening, coordination, and knowledge sharing.
- Facilitate programme development, assessments, evaluations, research initiatives, and fundraising opportunities for regional programmes.
- Represent Danish Red Cross in relevant regional coordination forums, partnerships, and technical networks.

As Regional Programme Coordinator, you will become part of a team of passionate colleagues in the MENA Regional Office. The Regional Office is responsible for strategic programme development, technical support, partnership management, humanitarian response, organizational development, and support the proposal development across the region. Teamwork, ambitions, and collaboration are key elements of our everyday work, while maintaining a strong focus on quality, accountability, innovation, and results.

As Regional Programme Coordinator, you will report to the Deputy Head of Region, MENA.

The position will be based in Amman, Jordan.

**We believe that you fit this position if:**

- You have a minimum of 7 years of experience in programme management, project implementation, or humanitarian and development programming.
- You hold a relevant postgraduate degree in Health or another relevant discipline related to programme management, public health, humanitarian action, or international development.
- You have proven experience managing multi-country programmes in development and/or conflict-affected settings.
- You have demonstrated experience in project cycle management, monitoring and evaluation, donor reporting, and financial oversight.
- You possess excellent English communication and writing skills.
- Knowledge of Arabic is an asset.
- You have strong coordination, facilitation, networking, and relationship-building skills.
- You are comfortable working in culturally and politically sensitive environments and can manage competing priorities effectively.
- You are proficient in standard IT applications, including Microsoft Office tools.
- Experience in health programming, migration, protection, or disaster management is considered an advantage.
- Experience working with the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement is a strong assets.

**You will become part of the World's largest humanitarian organization**

The Red Cross Red Crescent Movement is the world's largest humanitarian organization. We help people on both sides of a conflict and in the remotest corners of the world, regardless of their religion, race or political views. The Red Cross is always there. We save lives every day, and we equip people with the tools they need to get through crises and disasters. We are part of your local community no matter where you live. With your help, we can be wherever we are needed, always.

International Department in the Danish Red Cross supports vulnerable people in Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East in close cooperation with Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in more than 20 countries and manages an annual turnover of more than 1 billion Danish kroner. We work specifically on strengthening preparedness and response capacities and implement both long-term development interventions and emergency response programmes within health, disaster preparedness and humanitarian action.

We offer meaningful work in a purpose-driven organization with highly engaged colleagues. We focus on professional development, employee well-being, flexibility, and a collaborative work environment where everyone contributes to delivering impactful humanitarian results.

This recruitment is for international profiles. For further information regarding the job, see the [job description](https://rodekors.emply.com/api-v2/shared-files/4ceb1c0e-84d8-466e-aea3-18eeb3503f4a/shared-access-keys/41rb5u6us5yaa99jd4ypwy64w1zeuj8rx5izkbbgvwyc98s5ov224ip8wfvc9st3). The contract duration is **two years**, with the possibility of extension. We offer seven weeks of holiday per year and cover accommodation in Amman.

This position includes regional travel, estimated at approximately **30-60 travel days per year**.

The contract will be administered in accordance with the Danish Red Cross [Terms and Conditions for Delegates](https://rodekors.emply.com/api-v2/shared-files/87f32d89-f812-4ded-a44f-c326949f1c9d/shared-access-keys/fhgj95ihhqmh5w3sqsst7zhqiyhjy74i6zs9ugqfa7k2lmi4umm28knittf9v6a6).

We look forward to hearing from you!

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical and operational leadership for the regional and inter-regional operationalisation of IOM’s RteBA, in line with its institutional framework, and in coordination with relevant COs, Regional Offices (ROs), HQ divisions and global RteBA coordination structures; lead the development and implementation of multi-country, multi-partner operational plans for relevant routes; and ensure coherence with IOM’s institutional priorities, relevant regional strategies, and country-level operational realities.
2. Oversee the region’s RteBA Flexible Funding Mechanism allocation and other assigned RteBA projects, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery against approved results frameworks, workplans, budgets, indicators and donor requirements; monitor overall implementation and take or recommend corrective action to address delivery, quality and resource issues.
3. Serve as the RO’s RteBA focal point and lead the region’s engagement and participation in the global RteBA Task Force and, together with specific RTSs, its workstreams. Ensure that regional needs and priorities are reflected in global instruments, deliver agreed regional inputs on schedule, and lead the testing of operational guidance in the region.
4. In close coordination with RPLOs and relevant COs, lead government engagement on the RteBA to anchor route-based action in the priorities of States along relevant migration routes and reflect those priorities in regional cooperation processes. Provide route-level analysis, strategic advice and positioning to regional consultative processes, cross-regional discussions, and intergovernmental dialogues.
5. Support the Policy and Liaison Unit in providing substantive and coordination support to the Regional United Nations Network on Migration (RUNNM), including developing activities, promoting complementarity, and facilitating information exchange among regional RUNNM structures, the UNNM at the global level, IOM’s internal route-based coordination arrangements, and other relevant regional and inter-regional mechanisms.
6. In coordination with the Regional Director and Deputy Regional Director, lead the development and maintenance of strategic partnerships in support of the RteBA with United Nations (UN) agencies, international and national Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), civil society, migrant- and community-led organisations, academia, the private sector and other relevant actors. Provide substantive advice on partnership opportunities and approaches in support of regional RteBA priorities.
7. In close coordination with RPDOs and relevant RTSs, lead the coordination of coherent and integrated RteBA programming across global, regional and country levels, ensuring alignment of programme concepts, proposals and funding approaches through effective coordination with relevant technical and operational teams. Participate in the development of funding strategies and resource mobilisation initiatives, including through engagement with donors and strategic partners, and provide substantive inputs on regional funding priorities and opportunities.
8. In coordination with the relevant RTSs and the RPLOs, lead the translation of route-level analysis and operational experience into regional and inter-regional policy advice, practical guidance, capacity building priorities and coordinated support for Member States, UN Country Teams (UNCT) and country networks.
9. Lead efforts to strengthen institutional capacity and organisational learning for route-based programming by supporting the development, adaptation and institutionalisation of RteBA tools, guidance, methodologies, standard operating procedures, knowledge products and good practices within IOM.
10. Establish and maintain route-level coordination mechanisms among IOM COs and, where relevant, other ROs along migration routes; convene regular route coordination meetings; provide route-level guidance; and oversee the implementation of agreed multi-country, multi-partner operational plans.
11. In coordination with RPDOs and Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officers (RPMEOs), coordinate the development and dissemination of route-level evidence, knowledge management products, diagnostic assessments, lessons learned and analytical outputs to support a shared understanding of priority migration routes, and formulate recommendations to inform regional programming and decision-making.
12. Contribute to institutional learning, results-based monitoring, donor engagement and strategic decision-making by leading the consolidation and communication of regional and route-level insights and providing substantive recommendations to inform programme priorities, implementation and policy development.
13. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master's degree in Political Science, Social Sciences, International Relations, Migration Studies, Development Studies, Law or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in migration policy and programme implementation coordination across multiple countries, preferably within IOM or the UN system;
- Experience in coordinating multi-stakeholder processes without line authority, including with governments, UN agencies, regional organisations and civil society;
- Experience in the design or application of analytical products (assessments, mobility or service mapping, diagnostics) in a migration context;
- Experience in donor engagement, resource mobilisation, proposal development and results-based project management; and,
- Experience in engagement with regional economic communities, regional consultative processes, intergovernmental dialogue or the United Nations Network on Migration is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of IOM’s Route-Based Approach (RteBA) and its institutional framing, and of IOM’s strategic and planning instruments, including the Strategic Results Framework and regional strategies;
- Knowledge of migration governance frameworks, including the Migration Governance Indicators (MGI) and the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration;
- Knowledge of migration dynamics, actors and coordination structures along the region’s priority migration routes;
- Strong analytical, drafting and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to synthesise multi-country inputs into coherent products; and,
- Ability to work across reporting lines and to reconcile regional and Headquarters priorities.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23370 Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (DRD) for Operations and overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD), and the guidance of the Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery (DHRR) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) provides advice and supports the implementation of institutional policy from HQ in Country Offices (COs) across the Region. Specifically, the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) provides oversight, quality control, and thematic expertise to promote consistent, cohesive, and quality evidence-based programming. Together with other Regional Thematic Units (RTUs), the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) contributes to thought leadership on saving lives and protecting individuals on the move, driving solutions to displacement, and facilitating regular pathways for migration. The RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit also identifies regional opportunities and risks, fosters knowledge sharing, encourages policy and research development, and supports cross-thematic collaboration internally. Externally, the Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) offers advocacy, policy, and technical programme recommendations to regional entities, Member States, and relevant migration fora, spearheaded by IOM’s Regional Office (RO) and CO leadership. For both IOM teams and partners

in the region, the Regional Thematic Specialist Humanitarian Response and Recovery is the go-to source for humanitarian response and recovery expertise and guidance.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Advocacy, and Representation:**

1\. Strategic Direction: Lead and manage the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit in the delivery of regular thematic guidance and technical support to COs in the contextualization of the Strategic Plan.

2\. Advocacy and Representation: Assist and provide strategic advice to the DRD for Operations by articulating IOM's Strategic Plan to external stakeholders or in fora, discussions, and platforms, based on HQ and Global Offices' (GOs) guidance.

**Technical Support and Capacity Building:**

3\. Technical Assistance: Lead the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit's delivery of technical assistance on thematic and cross-cutting priorities based on identified or requested needs in collaboration with HQ and COs. Coordinate across regional units, relevant COs, and HQ for crisis responses, focusing on preparedness, protection in emergencies and AAP, life-saving actions, displacement tracking, peace, recovery and solutions.

4\. Training and Capacity Development: In coordination with HQ functional homes and the Staff Development and Learning Unit, provide thematic training and capacity building to COs and RO staff as well as external partners as requested.

**Partnerships and Resource Mobilization:**

5\. Strategic Partnerships: Develop and maintain partnerships with a diverse range of regional actors, including donors, regional political and economic bodies, UN, private sector, non-government institutions, academic institutions, community-based organizations, international financial institutions, international organizations, and Member States, to promote IOM’s Strategic Plan.

6\. Resource Mobilization: In coordination with HQ, GOs, Country Offices for Partnership and Advocacy, COs, and the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), advocate programmatic priorities with new and traditional donors, including the private sector.

**Quality Control and Oversight:**

7\. Project Development and Reporting: In coordination with the RPDOs, facilitate the project development and reporting process through technical inputs, review, approval, and endorsement in line with IOM’s Project Handbook and thematic guidance from DHRR HQ.

8\. Monitoring and Evaluation: In coordination with the Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, hold regular bilateral discussions with CO thematic focal points to assess

challenges, opportunities, and trends. Flag issues and opportunities to senior regional and HQ staff and guide COs' adjustments. Actively support COs to integrate audit, evaluation, and donor feedback. 9. Risk Management: In coordination with the Risk and Compliance Officer, provide oversight and support to COs on the identification, management, and treatment of risks pertaining to DHRR, in line with IOM's Risk Management Framework and Policy (IN/213 Rev.1).

10\. Cash-Based Interventions: In coordination with the global CBI Officer, promote the use of cash-based modalities, where feasible, in line with IOM's global strategies, standards and commitments, and provide guidance and support to COs in designing, implementing and coordinating CBI.

**Knowledge Management, Policy, and Research:**

11\. Knowledge Management and Innovation: In coordination with the RPDO, contribute to and facilitate the use of knowledge-sharing platforms, and disseminate innovative and best practices related to DHRR.

12\. Policy: In coordination with the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer, provide thematic support and recommendations on regional and country-level policies and frameworks to COs, donors, and key partners.

13\. Data, Research, and Foresight: In coordination with HQ and the Regional Data Hub, analyse and disseminate thematic data to inform evidence-based strategic planning, resource mobilization, policymaking, and programming.

**Communication and Coordination:**

14\. Thematic Community of Practice: Convene and maintain a community of practice in the region for thematic focal points in COs, with involvement of HQ functional homes as relevant, to promote sharing of new practices, innovative approaches, partnerships, training opportunities, and other areas of regional thematic interest.

15\. Coordination: Lead engagement in inter-regional, continental, and multi-country initiatives, programmes, and strategies with corresponding RTSs, Global Thematic Specialists, and CO focal points; where necessary, coordinate the involvement of HQ functional homes.

**Cross-Cutting Priorities:**

16\. Mainstream: In line with the IOM Strategic Plan and corresponding custodianship outlined in the Regional Office Terms of Reference, promote, integrate, and mainstream cross-cutting priorities and modalities (i.e., Cash-Based Interventions) in all areas of DHRR’s work in the region. The Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) is responsible for mainstreaming protection-centered approaches in all areas of IOM's work.

17\. Custodianship: The Regional Thematic Specialist (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) is the regional custodian of IOM’s Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion in humanitarian settings, AAP, and Cash-Based Initiatives. Custodianship entails support to other RTUs, as requested, with technical knowledge and capacity on protection mainstreaming as outlined under the Department of Humanitarian Response and Recovery Terms of Reference and the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit Terms of Reference.

**DHRR Regional Thematic Unit Management:**

18\. Manage the RO Humanitarian Response and Recovery Unit, including overseeing and managing the delivery of the Unit’s specific responsibilities in their entirety as outlined in the Unit’s Terms of Reference.

19\. Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Social Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with at least seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with at least nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in humanitarian response and recovery, and related areas relevant to project development and management, thematic capacity building, and liaison;
- Minimum five years experience working in non-OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) countries managing humanitarian response and recovery projects;
- Experience in liaison, resource mobilization, and advocacy with governmental and diplomatic officials, national and international institutions and organizations, civil society, and private sector actors;
- Experience working in an international, inter-governmental, or non-governmental organization, United Nations, or government; and,
- Experience in the design and implementation of capacity building on humanitarian response and recovery.

**Skills**

- Ability to understand complex contexts and fast-changing migration and displacement dynamics and ability to frame them in their regional, global, and political contexts;
- Proven track record of successful engagement with donors, developing projects, and mobilizing resources for IOM priority areas;
- Demonstrated ability to effectively lead and manage a diverse teams of specialists;
- Strong analytical skills combined with the ability to effectively summarize, present, and communicate findings;
- Demonstrated knowledge and expertise of relevant international standards and classifications relevant to humanitarian response and recovery; and,
- Proven agent of change or willingness to foster a culture of learning and knowledge management.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23396 Regional Programme Specialist (Regional Responses to Climate Displacement (RE2CLID)) (P)
body:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is the UN Migration Agency. With 175 member states, it is committed to the principle that humane and orderly migration benefits migrants and society. Established in 1951 and now active in over 400 field locations worldwide, IOM works with partners, governments, and civil society to:

1\. Assist in meeting the operational challenges of migration and human mobility;

2\. Advance understanding of migration issues;

3\. Encourage social and economic development through migration; and

4\. Uphold the human dignity and well-being of migrants.

Over the past years, IOM has worked closely with national and local authorities and communities across sub-Saharan Africa to address displacement, supporting the planning of and implementation of evacuation measures, the provision of humanitarian assistance to displaced populations, the coordination and management of sites hosting displaced communities, and promoting the achievement of durable solutions. IOM is also at the forefront of efforts to support the mainstreaming of migration into disaster preparedness, disaster response, disaster risk reduction, and climate change adaptation into continental, regional, and national development policies and plans, and actively engages with governments, communities, and local partners to build the resilience of communities to climate change.

In May 2023, representatives of the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA) of the European Commission began discussions on an action to be implemented under the Regional Multi-Annual Indicative Plan for Sub-Saharan Africa (RMIP SSA) for 2024, which resulted in the development of the “Regional Responses to Climate Displacement in Sub-Saharan Africa” programme (RE2CLID) outlining a regional response to climate displacement.

The RE2CLID programme seeks to enhance the resilience, self-reliance, and protection of Displacement-Affected Communities (DACs) living in areas at risk of disasters, environmental degradation, and the adverse effects of climate change. The programme operates across two highly vulnerable sub-regional clusters, inclusive of Cluster 1 - the Lake Tanganyika Basin, encompassing Burundi, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Tanzania, and Cluster 2 - the Southern Africa and South-West Indian Ocean region, including Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Mauritius, Seychelles, and Comoros. The objective of the programme is to improve overall capacity to respond to and increase overall resilience to disaster displacement at the regional level through strategic interventions regionally, nationally, and locally.

The action is framed around three main objectives: Strengthen systems that enable us to avert, minimize, and address displacement, and promote effective adaptation and resilience of communities most exposed to displacement risks due to climate hazards; Improve the governance and management of natural resources and agricultural land use in ways that create sustainable livelihoods for displaced and host communities; Help population displaced attain climate resilient durable solutions and enable social cohesion in host and return communities. By addressing the root causes of disaster-induced displacement and fostering inclusive, climate-resilient solutions, RE2CLID aims to reduce vulnerability and enhance long-term resilience in displacement-affected communities.

Under the direct supervision of the Regional Deputy Director for Operations, the overall supervision of the Regional Director for East Horn and Southern Africa, and in close coordination with Managing Missions and Country project teams, the Regional Thematic Specialists and the Global Office, the Regional Programme Specialist, Regional Responses to Climate Displacement (RE2CLID) will be responsible and accountable for the overall strategic and technical coordination of the RE2CLID programme to ensure the implementation of harmonized, coherent, and technically sound activities based on timely and informed decision-making at regional level. The Regional Programme Specialist, Regional Responses to Climate Displacement (RE2CLID), will also lead regional activities of the RE2CLID, supervise the Regional Support Team, act as the principal focal point for regional organizations, and serve as the primary liaison with the European Commission and other institutional partners at the regional level.

**Responsibilities**

1. Coordinate the implementation of the programme at the regional level and facilitate decision-making in a timely, harmonised/coherent, and informed manner at the level of action.
2. Lead the planning and implementation of regional activities and lead stakeholder engagement and partnership development at the regional level, and actively identify resource mobilization opportunities to complement, amplify the impact, and strengthen the sustainability of RE2CLID initiatives.
3. In coordination with the Managing Missions and Global Office (GO) Brussels, engage regularly with the European Commission on the overall programme strategy and orientation, participate in Regional Steering Committees, and provide high-level guidance on the development, implementation and adjustment of programme activities.
4. Work with Managing Missions to ensure alignment with donor requirements and compliance with IOM's institutional project management policies and procedures, including financial management, human resources, reporting, visibility, and risk management protocols.
5. Ensure the development and use of harmonized systems, procedures, and tools for the planning, implementation, and monitoring of the project, including budgets and annual workplans; provide capacity development to missions on their use, and provide troubleshooting in coordination with Cluster Management missions and relevant Regional Office (RO) and GO Units.
6. Provide day-to-day technical guidance and support to implementing missions, conduct regular in-country deployments, and ensure the integration of global policy directions and thematic innovations into RE2CLID programming, in coordination with Managing missions.
7. Identify needs for additional technical and programmatic support and mobilize internal and external resources as necessary in close coordination with the Managing missions, Regional Thematic Specialists, Regional Resource Management Unit, the Global Office and Headquarters (HQ) Units.
8. Support the integration of actions to address protection risks, including gender-based violence, and ensure the integration of inclusive approaches within all programme components regionally, emphasizing the active participation of women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, DACs, and marginalized groups.
9. Provide guidance on the development of area-based approaches and localization of activities implemented to ensure the sustainability of actions and the development of exit strategies.
10. Facilitate timely and coherent communication and information sharing across clusters, conduct cross-cluster trend analysis and promote cross-cluster and institutional learning, including by preparing policy inputs and capturing lessons from implementation at the regional level.
11. Supervise the Regional Support Team, regularly track progress made in the implementation of the action in coordination with Managing Missions, support problem-solving and escalate any high-level unresolved issues for timely decision-making.
12. Convene and lead the Internal Programme Committee to ensure cross-cluster coordination and strategic alignment, and participate in the RE2CLID Senior Management Team meeting to raise unresolved issues and ensure high-level decision-making in coordination with the Deputy Regional Director.
13. Represent IOM and RE2CLID in related regional and global strategic forums, lead advocacy and visibility efforts at the regional level, and ensure the implementation of an effective external communication strategy of programme achievements and lessons learned, in close coordination with Cluster Managing Missions, the European Union Delegations (EUDs), Country managers and IOM’s Media and Communication Department.
14. Serve as the primary liaison with key regional partners, including but not limited to Regional Economic Communities, Regional Organizations, Regional Offices of the UN, Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGO), Multilateral Banks, etc.
15. Ensure coordination with other IOM offices and programmes not directly included in RE2CLID, identifying synergies, sharing tools, and supporting institutional coherence on disaster preparedness, disaster response, disaster risk reduction, climate action and durable solutions to increase impact of the RE2CLID initiative regionally.
16. Guide Cluster Managing missions with the drafting and timely submission of periodic progress reports, briefings, and other documents, and ensure accurate documentation of RE2CLID programme achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and best practices at regional level
17. Ensure the implementation of baseline, midline, and endline assessments regionally.
18. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in international development, International Relations, Social Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Disaster Management, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with at least seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with at least nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Significant experience in programme management and coordination, including multi-country or regional programmes on disaster preparedness, disaster response, displacement management, disaster risk reduction, and durable solutions is essential;
- Extensive operational experience in contexts affected by displacement due to crises – including disasters and conflict - is essential;
- Significant experience in developing and implementing area-based and localization strategies is essential;
- Extensive experience in coordinating multi-country actions, supervising diverse and multicultural teams, managing technical backstopping structures, and coordinating programme support functions across countries; and,
- Strong expertise covering a wide range of thematic areas, particularly those related to displacement management, emergency preparedness, emergency response, disaster risk reduction, durable solutions, climate change adaptation, and environmental governance; with at least six years of relevant experience in displacement crisis and post-crisis contexts.

**Skills**

- Proven expertise in designing strategic guidance and operationalizing “whole of displacement” responses across the humanitarian, peace, and development nexus is essential;
- Demonstrated expertise in managing large-scale donor-funded initiatives, particularly with the European Union, including donor relations, strategic planning, visibility, and reporting;
- Proven ability to lead regional partnership development, policy engagement, and high-level representation, including with UN agencies, regional organizations, government entities, and civil society, in regional and global fora;
- Familiarity with regional cooperation mechanisms in areas targeted by the action is highly desirable;
- Demonstrated strategic leadership and coordination skills in complex, multi-stakeholder environments, with sound judgment and the ability to make timely, informed decisions;
- Capacity to analyse and synthesize technical and policy information and to translate complex concepts into actionable strategies, plans, and guidance;
- Proven ability to maintain flexibility and professionalism under pressure, and to adapt quickly to changing priorities and evolving circumstances;
- Excellent interpersonal and representational skills, including the ability to communicate effectively, negotiate diplomatically, and foster collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders; and,
- High proficiency in digital collaboration tools and office applications, including spreadsheets, databases, and knowledge management systems.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Portuguese and another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23395 Senior Programme Manager (Immigration and Border Governance (IBG)) (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director Operations and technical oversight of the Senior Regional Thematic Specialist (IBG), and in cooperation with relevant departments at Headquarters (HQs), the Senior Programme Manager (IBG) will be responsible and accountable for the overall coordination and management of the Regional Counter Migrant Smuggling Programme (RCMSP), including strengthening the capacity of participating border management agencies and IOM Country Offices (COs) to respond to emerging challenges in counter migrant smuggling and border management, contributing to stronger migration governance and border security in the region. The Senior Programme Manager will oversee all aspects of the Programme development and implementation, including but not limited to monitoring, reporting, capacity building, extensive high-level stakeholder liaison, staff supervision, and advancement of new initiatives within the Programme and in a global context. In addition, the Senior Programme Manager will contribute to IOM's global programming on counter migrant smuggling, including the Data Exchange Solution for Counter Migrant Smuggling (DESC) and supporting other regional and global-level engagements on the subject. The Senior Programme Manager will oversee the programme management functions and will provide expert support and advice for the development of strategic plans at the regional office on countering migrant smuggling and border management.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide strategic oversight and management of the RCMSP, in line with IOM policies and practices as well as donor requirements, to ensure progress toward intended results, promote successful practices for replication, and address underperformance with corrective measures.
2. Provide leadership and ensure coordination of RCMSP interventions across and between COs implementing project activities, different organizational units, and technical divisions at HQs.
3. Coordinate the design and implementation of contextualized capacity building activities on counter migrant smuggling and related migration and border management thematic areas, targeting relevant institutions, as well as project staff, in collaboration with relevant technical specialists and partners.
4. Consult regularly with key internal and external stakeholders, including CO focal persons, technical specialists, programme staff, donor representatives, and government representatives, to refine strategy; build synergies with other ongoing national, regional, and/ or global related initiatives, and ensure programme visibility.
5. Establish strong working relationships at national and regional levels, including with relevant government counterparts and regional authorities, and participate in relevant counter migrant smuggling and border management-related engagements to enhance awareness of IOM's capacities in the counter migrant smuggling field and pursue increased cooperation with key stakeholders such as relevant UN agencies, international organizations, NGOs, academia, and the private sector.
6. Identify emerging needs and priorities in counter migrant smuggling to expand programming in the region in coordination with Senior Regional Thematic Specialist (SRTS), COs, relevant government partners, and other stakeholders.
7. Ensure Programme compliance with IOM's project management policies, including HR, financial management, donor reporting, and risk management.
8. Support creation of a culture of monitoring, evaluation, and learning within the Programme. Encourage  
    identification of lessons learned and best practices, promote action-oriented research, and facilitate real-time incorporation of knowledge and learning into Programme implementation.
9. Supervise and direct project/ programme staff; oversee and coordinate, as required, the recruitment of programme staff and consultants.
10. Participate in or lead field missions and other duty travel related to project implementation, monitoring and assessment, liaison with counterparts, and any other task as necessary in order to achieve project objectives.
11. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master's degree in Management, Social Science, Law, International Relations, Regional Studies, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience, or;
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in managing large, multicountry projects/ programmes (notably in the fields of migration, border management, law enforcement);
- Experience in the field of migration and border management, including policy and operational experience;
- Background in immigration and border management, including border management technologies, Integrated Border Management, and capacity building in migration and border management;
- Demonstrated managerial experience in staff management;
- Proven record of establishing and maintaining good working relationships with governmental and diplomatic authorities, national, regional, and international institutions, international agencies (i.e., UN), and civil society organizations;
- Experience in project development, implementation, and reporting, including financial and budgetary aspects; and,

- Strong communication skills, including good oral and written English as well as good computer skills (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint);

- Efficiency, flexibility, a high level of professionalism, and the ability to adhere to strict deadlines; and,
- Strong leadership, management, and coordination capacity.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).
