title: 23266 Regional Migration Health Nurse Coordinator (P)
body:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Health Assessment Programme Coordinator (DRHAPC), the Regional Migration Health Nurse Coordinator will be responsible for substantively supporting Migration Health Division’s (MHD) nursing leadership structure and for carrying out the following duties and responsibilities in relation to the Migration Health Assessment Programme across the region.

**Responsibilities**

1\. Establish and maintain an optimal workflow, efficiency, and client satisfaction in all migration health assessment nursing and clerical activities in the region to fulfil the technical requirements of the resettlement countries, including but not limited to:   
a) Medical examinations  
b) Imaging  
c) Laboratory testing  
d) Vaccinations  
e) TB management  
f) Treatment and referrals  
g) Pre-departure procedures and medical movements  
h) Counselling  
i) Infection prevention and control  
j) Documentation, certification and information transmission  
k) Other technical areas as may be required

2\. Provide technical advice and coordination for vaccination programmes across regional HAP operations, including vaccine policy implementation, operational oversight, performance monitoring, and alignment with global MHD vaccination strategies.

3\. Backstop and monitor resource management in Health Assessment Programmes (HAP) in the following areas:  
a) In coordination with DRHAPC, recommend staffing levels for nurses and support staff, contribute to the harmonization of grades and post descriptions, and provide advice to senior regional MHD colleagues and the Chief Migration Health Officer (CHMO) on optimal staffing levels and organization of nursing and support staff.  
b) Participate in recruitment of nurses, especially in leadership positions such as Migration Health Nurse Officer (MHNO) and/or Senior Nurses.  
c) Promote and support the use of the Medical Inventory Management System for medications and medical supplies in collaboration with pharmacists, MHNO/senior nurses, and CMHO in the Region.  
d) Provide regional oversight of cold chain systems, including equipment standards, temperature monitoring, contingency planning, and corrective actions.  
e) Coordinate with pharmacists, supply chain colleagues, and country teams to ensure end-to-end vaccine availability and integrity, including during surge and mobile operations.  
f) Design, apply, and oversee regional monitoring and evaluation tools for vaccination programmes, including analysis of vaccine coverage, consumption, wastage, refusal rates, and cold chain performance across countries.  
g) Consolidate and analyse regional vaccination data and prepare regular regional reports for DRHAPC and MHD Headquarters (HQ), highlighting trends, risks, and corrective actions.  
h) Facilitate the development of an Asset Management System related to medical equipment, in coordination with relevant stakeholders.  
i) Assist DRHAPC in budget reviews towards the adequacy of human and material resources for programme implementation.  
j) Maintain an optimal staff flow, including the allocation to routine duties, staff leave planning and work handover in regional mobile unit.

4\. Promote the implementation of best practice standards as they relate to nursing activities within HAP operations by developing and instructing best practice guidelines, evidence-based clinical standards, and supporting the development and implementation of standard operating procedures as they relate to nursing practice.

5\. Coordinate and facilitate nurse education programs, using a variety of learning techniques, including:

a) Develop entry-on-duty and refresher training programmes and guidelines/Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for nurses in the region.  
b) Oversee the development and delivery of vaccination-specific training, including safe administration practices, cold chain management, Adverse Event Following Immunization (AEFI) recognition, documentation standards, and counselling.  
c) Organize in-house and external training and keep track of nurses’ engagement in training and continuous medical education.

6\. Coordinate clear communication strategies for the sharing of clinical practice resources and information to support HAP operations.

7\. Monitor clinical practice across HAP operations using standardized auditing tools and provide feedback on clinical and workflow performance, in respect of principle nursing procedures. Suggest corrective actions while analyzing and disseminating best practices.

8\. Serve as Regional Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Officer; support the implementation of IPC standards in IOM medical facilities; contribute to the development of such policies.

9\. Coordinate and oversee AEFI surveillance at regional level, ensuring standardized reporting, investigation follow-up, and escalation pathways in coordination with CMHOs and MHD HQ.

10\. Monitor epidemiological trends relevant to vaccine-preventable diseases in HAP populations and advise DRHAPC and CMHOs on operational implications for vaccination delivery, in alignment with global policies.

11\. Coordinate and implement a sound monitoring system of medical document flow and data entry; perform routine spot checks and apply quality assessment/quality control mechanisms to ensure errors are minimal in the relevant databases.

12\. Ensure that pharmacy, stock, medical kits, and emergency kits within the Region and for medical escorts, if applicable, are being monitored; perform spot checks to ensure that they are well maintained.

13\. Assess and recommend purchase of medical supplies; monitor inventory of medical supplies and verify that all Migration Health Assessment Clinics have clear SOP’s regarding medical supply procurement.

14\. In coordination with the Regional Medical Movement Coordinator, support regional pre-departure health activities, including oversight of treatment and pre-embarkation fitness-to-travel assessments as required; ensure appropriate documentation and reporting; support follow-up actions for cases placed on medical hold after health assessment; and provide regional technical guidance on the management of Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) and tuberculosis treatment, including Directly Observed Therapy (DOT), in coordination with country-level teams.

15\. Prepare and finalize medical and administrative reports and program updates as necessary; report any inconsistencies or issues on the regional level to relevant CMHOs and DRHAPC.

16\. Plan and organize mobile or surge missions, if applicable, and supervise communication with the non-IOM panel physicians with regard to the follow-up on the cooperation with non-IOM Panel Physicians in PDMS procedures, surveillance, fitness for travel, the vaccination process, and the service provider agreements with non-IOM Panel Physicians and service providers.

17\. Provide technical and administrative support to the DRHAPC and/or relevant CMHOs in the planning, coordination, and delivery of all regional migration health programmes. This includes the collation and consolidation of data, information, and operational plans related to programme implementation across the region, and the translation of these inputs into coordinated regional action plans.

18\. Contribute to technical medical oversight, planning, monitoring, and follow-up of IOM migration health assessment programmes in the region, including surge missions, temporary deployments, and activities conducted in remote or non-routine locations. Ensure that these programmes meet the technical requirements of resettlement countries, including standardization and the application of Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) across all aspects of the medical examination and documentation process:  
**•**  In particular, support the planning and coordination of regional health assessment activities for surge or remote operations, in collaboration with Heads of Migration Health Assessment Centres and relevant country teams, ensuring appropriate coverage in locations without permanent IOM MHD presence, as well as cost-effectiveness, monitoring, and performance oversight in coordination with the DRHAPC.

19\. Coordinate, and perform if needed, the medical escort duties when required to ensure migrants receive continued care throughout all phases of migration (before departure, during the journey and at the final destination).

20\. Establish and maintain collaborative relationships with various partners to facilitate the follow-up and relevant information sharing. Partners include internal IOM departments, other health providers, panel physicians, embassies, other UN agencies or Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and others as applicable.

21\. Prepare, compile, and finalize relevant survey and statistical information and share with the DRHAPC as per pre-set and agreed-upon format.

22\. Perform other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Nursing from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience with at least two years in a management role; or,
- University degree in the above field with seven years of relevant clinical experience with three years in a management role.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Working experience in the areas of Tuberculosis management, mass immunizations, communicable diseases, laboratory testing, or public health is an advantage;
- Demonstrated experience in implementation of QC/QA principles is mandatory;
- Experience in developing guidelines and instructions for nursing services is desirable;
- Knowledge and experience of using IOM Databases and Application is an advantage; and,
- Previous international experience in HAP is a distinctive advantage.

**Skills**

- Nursing experience in international and national settings;
- Involvement in review and accreditation of nursing degrees and diplomas;
- Demonstrated senior-level managerial skills are mandatory; and,
- Computer literacy required: MS Office suite (Word, Excel, Access).

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 23423 Regional Thematic Specialist (Climate Action and Mobility) (P)
body:
Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (DRD) for Operations, the overall supervision of the Regional Director (RD), and the guidance of the Climate Action Division (CAD) in Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Thematic Specialist on Climate Action and Mobility (CAD RTS) provides advice and support to the implementation of institutional policies from HQ to Country Offices (COs) across the Region. Specifically, the Regional Thematic Specialist provides oversight, quality control, and thematic and operational support to promote consistent, cohesive, and quality evidence-based programming. Together with other Regional Thematic Units (RTUs), the Regional Thematic Specialist on Climate Action and Mobility contributes to thought leadership on saving lives and protecting individuals on the move, driving solutions to displacement, and facilitating regular pathways for migration.

The Regional Thematic Specialist will also lead the CAD RTU, which will provide thematic oversight and support on regional efforts to address the immediate and long-term impacts of climate change on human mobility while advocating sustainable and inclusive solutions on a regional scale in collaboration with CAD HQ. Special focus will be placed on leveraging IOM’s expertise and role in the new Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage and access to climate financing and technical support to Member States on National Adaptation Plans (NAP) and National Determination Commitments (NDC), especially for Small Islands Developing States and Least Developed Countries that experience interconnected social, environmental and economic challenges. The CAD RTU will also identify regional opportunities and risks, foster knowledge sharing, encourage policy and research development, and support cross-thematic collaboration internally. Externally, the CAD RTU offers advocacy, policy, and technical programme recommendations to regional entities, Member States, and relevant migration fora, spearheaded by IOM’s Regional Office (RO) and CO leadership. For both IOM teams and partners in the Region, the CAD RTU is the go-to source for climate action and mobility expertise and guidance.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Advocacy, and Representation:**

1\. **Strategic Direction:** Lead and manage the CAD RTU in the delivery of regular thematic guidance and technical support to COs in the contextualization of the strategic plan.

2\. **Advocacy and Representation:** Assist and provide substantive inputs to the DRD for Operations by articulating IOM's strategic plan to external stakeholders or in fora, discussions, and platforms, based on CAD HQ and Global Offices' (GO) guidance.

**Technical Support and Capacity Building:**

3\. **Technical Assistance:** Lead the CAD RTU's delivery of technical assistance on thematic and cross-cutting priorities based on identified or requested needs in collaboration with CAD HQ and COs. Coordinate across regional units, relevant COs, and HQ for crisis responses, focusing on Climate change and human mobility, protection, life-saving actions, and recovery.

4\. **Training and Capacity Development:**  
a. In coordination with CAD HQ and the Staff Development and Learning Unit, provide thematic training and capacity building to COs and RO staff as well as external partners as requested.  
b. Spearhead the consultation, development, consensus-building, implementation, and oversight of global Climate migration and displacement governance frameworks across member states, international organizations, and civil society on the global stage.  
c. In coordination with and in support of COs, strengthen the technical and institutional capacity of national governments and local actors to absorb, account for, report on, allocate, and leverage climate finance effectively.

**Partnerships and Resource Mobilization:**

5\. **Strategic Partnerships:** Develop and maintain partnerships with a diverse range of regional actors, including donors, regional political and economic bodies, UN, private sector, non-government institutions, academic institutions, community-based organizations, international financial institutions, international organizations, and Member States, to promote IOM’s Strategic Plan.

6\. **Resource Mobilization:** In coordination with HQ, GOs, Country Offices for Partnerships and Advocacy (COPAs), COs, and the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), advocate programmatic priorities with new and traditional donors, including the private sector.

**Quality Control and Oversight:**

7\. **Project Development and Reporting:** In coordination with the RPDOs, facilitate the project development and reporting process through technical inputs, review, approval, and endorsement in line with IOM’s Project Handbook.

8\. **Monitoring and Evaluation:** In coordination with the Regional Planning, Monitoring, and Evaluation Officer (RPMEO), hold regular bilateral discussions with COs thematic focal points to assess challenges, opportunities, and trends. Flag issues and opportunities to senior regional and HQ staff, and guide CO adjustments. Actively support COs to integrate audit, evaluation, and donor feedback.

9\. **Risk Management:** In coordination with the Risk and Compliance Officer, provide oversight and support to COs on the identification, management, and treatment of risks pertaining to DHRR, in line with IOM's Risk Management Framework and Policy (IN/213 Rev.1).

**Climate Action Policy and Research:**

10\. **Knowledge Management and Innovation:** In coordination with the RPDO and Climate Mobility Innovation Labs Unit, contribute to and facilitate the use of knowledge-sharing platforms, and disseminate Climate Action innovative and best practices related to CAD.

11\. **Policy:**  
a. Promote policy coherence and inclusive partnerships to mainstream climate mobility in relevant agendas, including biodiversity, water management, mountains, oceans/seas, human rights, protection, security, gender, health, urbanization, SDGs, youth engagement, diaspora empowerment, local actors’ mobilization.  
b. Scale up advocacy, policy, and partnership in early warning (EW4AI), and climate and environmental action at policy and advocacy levels, in support of priorities identified by affected countries in national or regional and global climate strategies.  
c. Support CAD HQ in the mainstreaming of human mobility considerations in climate change, environmental and disaster policy agendas, including via its work on UNFCCC Constituted Bodies, Workstreams, Initiatives and Fora (WIM Excom, AC, SNLD, COP, NAPs, NDCs, climate funds, etc.), as well as the UNCCD, UNEA and Sendai Framework policy processes, and the engagement with the Climate Vulnerable Forum (CVF).

12\. **Data, Research, and Foresight:** In coordination with different climate change fora including UNFCCC, IPCC, IDMC and others in collaboration with CAD HQ, as well as the Global Data Institute (GDI), and the Regional Data Hub (RDH), analyse and disseminate Climate Action thematic data to inform evidence-based strategic planning, resource mobilization, policymaking, and programming.

**Communication and Coordination:**

13\. **Thematic Community of Practice:** Convene and maintain a community of practice in the region for thematic focal points in COs, with involvement of CAD HQ functional homes as relevant, to promote sharing of new practices, innovative approaches, partnerships, training opportunities, and other areas of regional thematic interest.

14\. **Coordination:** Lead engagement in inter-regional, continental, and multi-country initiatives, programmes, and strategies with corresponding RTS, Global Thematic Specialists (GTS), and COs focal points; where necessary, coordinate the involvement of HQ functional homes.

**Cross-Cutting Priorities:**

15\. **Mainstream:** In line with the IOM Strategic Plan and corresponding custodianship outlined in the Regional Office Terms of Reference, promote, integrate, and mainstream cross-cutting priorities in all areas of CAD’s work in the Region. Furthermore, promote the integration of Climate Action at RO and CO levels to enhance programme leadership, strategy, design and implementation across all thematic areas.

**CAD Regional Thematic Unit Management:**

16\. Manage the CAD Regional Thematic Unit, including overseeing and managing the delivery of the Unit’s specific responsibilities in their entirety as outlined in the CAD RTU Terms of Reference.

17\. Perform any other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Social Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with at least seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with at least nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the [UNESCO World Higher Education Database](https://whed.net/home.php).

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in climate action and mobility, and related areas relevant to project development and management, thematic capacity building, and liaison;
- Minimum 5 years' experience working in non-OECD countries managing climate action and mobility projects;
- Experience in liaison, resource mobilization, and advocacy with governmental and diplomatic officials, national and international institutions and organizations, civil society, and private sector actors;
- Experience working in an international, inter-governmental, or non-governmental organization, the United Nations, or government; and,
- Experience in the design and implementation of capacity building on climate action and mobility.

**Skills**

- Ability to understand complex contexts and fast-changing migration and displacement dynamics and ability to frame them in their regional, global, and political contexts;
- Proven track record of successful engagement with donors, developing projects, and mobilizing resources for IOM priority areas;
- Demonstrated ability to effectively lead and manage a diverse teams of specialists;
- Strong analytical skills combined with the ability to effectively summarize, present, and communicate findings;
- Demonstrated knowledge and expertise of relevant international standards and classifications relevant to climate action and mobility; and,
- Proven agent of change or willingness to foster a culture of learning and knowledge management.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Portuguese and other official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

title: 22519 Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) (P)
body:
The Transition and Recovery (TR) Pillar of the Somalia Country Office plays a leading role in stabilisation strategy and delivery throughout Somalia. The Community Stabilisation programme is central to the United Nations (UN) Country Team’s plans for transition and closure of the UN’s political mission in Somalia. The main objective of the unit is to lead coordinated stabilisation efforts across the international community, aligned with the core objectives of the Government of Somalia.

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Sub-Office in Nairobi/Senior Programme Coordinator (Transition & Recovery Pillar) and the direct supervision of the Senior Programme Coordinator (Community Stabilisation), and in close coordination with the Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS) at the Regional Office (RO) for Eastern and Southern Africa in Nairobi and relevant Divisions/Departments/Units at Headquarters (HQ), the Programme Manager (Community Stabilisation) will be responsible and accountable for managing, coordinating and overseeing the activities of the European Union flagship stabilisation project: Strengthening the Social Contract through Socio-Economic Infrastructure (2026-2029), and its integration with the FCDO flagship project: Strengthening Community Security and Stabilisation (SCSS). title: Development of E-Learning Module Content — Tdh Migration and Displacement programme
body:
## **1. Background**

Terre des hommes (Tdh) is Switzerland's largest child rights organisation, active in over 30 countries. Its Migration and Displacement sector has developed two evidence-based Models of Action (MoA) to guide Tdh staff and partners working with migrant, displaced and at-risk children and youth:

**MoA 1 — Employability and access to employment for young migrants and refugees:** Employability and access to employment through (1) Skills and capabilities development, (2) Labour market linkage, and (3) Policy and system strengthening.

**MoA 2 — Education for children and youth on the move:** Structured around the 4As (Availability, Accessibility, Acceptability, Adaptability), leading to empowerment and socio-economic (re)integration.

Tdh wishes to make these frameworks accessible to its staff and implementing partners through the **development of related self-paced e-learning modules**. Tdh already runs a Migration and Displacement e-learning course for staff: the two new modules will be produced in the same format and uploaded to the existing platform by Tdh. This assignment covers content development only as platform integration is handled internally.

## **2. Objective and scope of work**

The consultant will develop content for two standalone e-learning modules, one for each MoA. The modules are intended for individual, self-paced learners. For each module, the consultant will submit a complete Word script that Tdh's technical team can upload to the existing CYM e-learning platform. The assignment does not include visual design, coding, platform configuration or upload work

**2.1 Consultant deliverables**

For each of the two modules, the consultant will deliver the following:

- Full content script (Word document): A complete, structured module script covering all learning content, activities and resources. The script must follow the format of the existing Tdh Migration and Development module series and be clear enough for Tdh's technical team to translate it into the online platform. It must include section text, activity instructions, external resource links with precise timecodes where relevant, correct answers for exercises, definitions and call-out boxes. It must be sufficiently clear and structured for the technical team to identify content blocks, activity types, correct answers, feedback text and any resources to be embedded or linked.
- Glossary: A list of 10-15 key terms with concise, learner-friendly definitions tailored to the thematic focus of the module.
- Learner summary sheet: A one-page printable reference sheet summarising the module's key concepts and takeaways, suitable for download alongside the module.
- Review and revision: The consultant will take part in an iterative review process, incorporate consolidated feedback from Tdh and submit revised versions until the module content is validated within the agreed workplan and timeline.

**2.2 Module format, components and minimum requirements**

Existing Migration and Development module scripts will be shared with the selected consultant as a formatting and style reference at the start of the assignment. Each module should follow the expected approach and minimum requirements below.

**Component**

1. Learner experience. **Expected approach:** Individual, self-paced learning. Content should be structured into short thematic sections that combine explanation, examples and activities. **Minimum requirement per module:** 45–60 minutes of learning time.
2. Narrative and voice. **Expected approach:** Write directly to the individual learner in the second person, using a clear and accessible register suitable for practitioners with varied educational backgrounds and operating contexts. **Minimum requirement per module** : Consistent second-person learner voice throughout the script.
3. Script length.**Expected approach :** Provide enough detail for direct platform integration, including all section text, activity instructions, answer keys and feedback text. **Minimum requirement per module** 2,500–4,000 words, including activity instructions and answers.
4. External resources. **Expected approach :** Curate publicly accessible, up-to-date and directly relevant resources, such as short videos, interactive data tools, websites, maps, reports or other practical materials. For any video used, provide precise start and end timecodes.**Minimum requirement per module** : Relevant external resources selected according to the learning objectives and availability of suitable materials. Each resource must include guided comprehension questions and correct answers where appropriate.
5. Interactive activities.**Expected approach :** Embed activities throughout the script and describe them clearly for platform build. Suitable formats include flip cards, matching or association exercises, multiple-choice questions, fill-in-the-blank questions and open reflection prompts. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 interactive activities, plus at least 1 open reflection prompt. Correct answers and short feedback text must be provided where relevant.
6. Case studies.**Expected approach :** Use real-world or fictionalised case studies grounded in Tdh field contexts, including Asia, Africa and Europe/MENA where relevant. Cases should include named fictional or anonymised characters and guided analysis questions. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.
7. Glossary and key concepts. **Expected approach :** Define core terms in concise, learner-friendly language and use call-out boxes to reinforce critical concepts, legal definitions, common misconceptions and section takeaways.**Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.

## **3. Required profile**

## **Mandatory**

- Demonstrated experience writing e-learning content scripts or instructional materials for NGO or UN audiences
- Strong ability to translate programmatic frameworks into clear, engaging learning content for individual practitioners
- Capacity to identify and integrate high-quality external resources (videos, data tools, reports) into a structured learning narrative
- Substantive knowledge in at least one of the two thematic areas: youth employability, education in emergencies / migration
- Excellent written English; ability to write in a direct, accessible register suitable for diverse field staff

### **Advantageous**

- Familiarity with child rights frameworks and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
- Knowledge of all two thematic areas covered by the MoAs

title: Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment
body:
Terms of reference (TOR)

Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment

UGANDA & KENYA

· Project: Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP)

· Procuring Organisation: IsraAID

· Contract Type: Consultancy

· Contract Period: October 2026 to December 2026, 75 days (Phased implementation)

· Target Start Date: Tentatively 26/10/2026

· Application Deadline: 23/10/2026

· Submission Method: EMAIL – see 'how to apply'

BACKGROUND

IsraAID is an International Humanitarian Non-Governmental Organization founded in 2001 and headquartered in Israel. It supports people and communities affected by humanitarian crises, combining rapid emergency response with longer-term recovery, resilience, and preparedness. Over the years, IsraAID has worked in more than 60 countries, responding to disasters, displacement, epidemics, and other crises. Its mission is centered on partnering closely with local communities to provide urgent assistance while helping them rebuild and strengthen their resilience to future shocks.

IsraAID is implementing a project titled Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement in Uganda and in Kakuma Refugee Camp in Kenya. The programme intends to improve health outcomes and reduce morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition in vulnerable communities participating in the Program. ICNMP is designed as a regional initiative that responds to acute and chronic nutrition needs across East Africa, beginning its phase zero in Q2 of 2026, and actual implementation in September 2026. Although the immediate program launch focuses on Uganda and the emergency phase in Kenya, early 2027 will see Kenya incorporating the full package while the broader intention is to establish a model that can later expand to South Sudan as funding becomes available. The regional framing is essential, as the scale of displacement, vulnerability, and recurring shocks across these countries requires harmonized technical standards, shared learning, and coordinated supply chain approaches. The program will expand decentralized nutrition services by placing screening, early identification, and treatment within spaces that families already use daily, including schools, Child-Friendly Spaces, transit points, and primary health facilities. To be able to achieve the intended outcomes, IsraAID seeks services of a consultant to conduct a baseline upon which project progress and successes will be measured.

This Terms of Reference (ToR) sets out the background, purpose, objectives, scope of work, expected deliverables, and management arrangements for the baseline study, and invites eligible firms to submit technical and financial proposals for consideration.

PURPOSE

This assignment aims at establishing both quantitative and qualitative baseline information on access to integrated nutrition services, nutrition and food security practices and programme systems to ensure that these are addressed by programme interventions to realise the intended overall goal. The baseline will also establish baseline information on several learning areas under the OECD criteria and the IsraAID Community Resilience framework (CRF). The baseline therefore aims at obtaining verified, disaggregated benchmark values for the programme indicators, enabling precise measurement of outcomes and impacts at endline (Year 2, 2028).

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The assignment will specifically

A. Assess the 3 programme outcome indicators

1\. Vulnerable communities — especially children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) — access integrated, quality nutrition services delivered through a multi-tier workforce (community and formal system) and functional multi-sectoral pathways.

2\. Caregivers and community structures adopt improved nutritional and food security practices that prevent and protect against malnutrition.

3\. Programme systems — accountability, information, governance and supply chain, inventory management systems, logistics & distribution modalities — are functional and progressively integrated into and owned by national, district and community structures.

B. Provide baseline information on the specified Community Resilience Framework (CRF) and OECD learning questions.

SCOPE

The baseline survey will be conducted in programme’s area of implementation, covering Nakivale Refugee Settlement and its surrounding host communities in Western Uganda and Turkana West Sub-County specifically targeting Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kalobeyei settlement and its surrounding host communities in Kenya. There are several credible data sources that will benefit the project including, among others, District Information Health System (DHIS 2),

Food Security and Nutrition Assessment reports (FSNA), Demographic Health Surveys, and Population Census reports. Primary baseline information will be obtained from, among others, health facilities, schools, households, children-friendly spaces, community structures and partners engaged in nutrition interventions

METHODOLOGY

IsraAID anticipates a mixed-methods baseline design combining quantitative and qualitative approaches, consistent with the evidence requirements set out in the MEAL Plan. The final design will be proposed by the Firm and refined collaboratively with IsraAID’s MEAL team.

The baseline study should be designed so that its instruments, sampling frame, and methodology can be replicated with fidelity at endline, enabling credible before and after comparison and contribution analysis.

ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS

The consultant will be expected to demonstrate how the assessment will be conducted in line with research ethics while protecting the human rights of the participants. It will also be the responsibility of the consultant to ensure strict adherence to IsraAID Safeguarding Policy. The consultant will also be responsible for ensuring that any persons hired, engaged, or consulted during the process are familiar with the policy and commit to abide by it during the delivery of the assignment.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE

This assignment will last approximately 75 days from the date of signing of the contract. The consultant will provide a detailed work plan with realistic timelines to the logical conclusion of the baseline survey. The following deliverables are expected from the consultant:

The baseline assessment will be undertaken by one consultant/firm. Fieldwork will be conducted sequentially, beginning in Uganda and subsequently moving to Kenya.

1\. Inception & Evaluation Design – Week 1

Key activities

· Desk review of programme proposal, Theory of Change, Logic Model and MEAL Plan.

· Inception meetings with IsraAID.

· Refine evaluation design, sampling strategy and evaluation matrix.

Deliverables

· Inception report.

· Refined methodology and sampling plan.

· Approved work plan and evaluation/indicator matrix.

2\. Tool Development, Piloting & Field Preparation – Weeks 2–3

Key activities

· Finalize quantitative and qualitative data collection tools aligned with Indicator Reference Sheets.

· Share tools with relevant teams and incorporate feedback.

· Pilot testing and tool refinement.

· Enumerator training/orientation and field preparation.

· Ethics/safeguarding clearance preparation.

Deliverables

· Approved final data collection tools and protocols.

· Pilot findings and revisions.

· Enumerator training/orientation completed.

· Ethics/safeguarding documentation.

3\. Data Collection – Uganda – Weeks 4–5

Key activities

· Deploy quantitative and qualitative surveys/interviews with agreed respondents in Uganda.

· Conduct ongoing field-level data quality assurance.

· Hold regular field debriefs with participating stakeholders.

· Complete Uganda fieldwork and initial data quality checks.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

Deliverables

· Uganda quantitative and qualitative data.

title: 23451 Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA) (P)
body:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director for Operations (DRD-O), and in close coordination with the Department of Mobility, Pathways and Inclusion (DMPI) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer (RPLO), the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs), and Country Offices (COs) along the region’s priority migration routes, the Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will be responsible and accountable for leading, at the technical level, the regional operationalisation and implementation of the IOM’s Route-Based Approach (RteBA) and providing strategic and programmatic advice on its implementation across the region.

The Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will ensure alignment with IOM’s global approach, lead regional and inter-agency coordination at the technical and operational levels, and oversee the application of Route-Based Approach (RteBA) tools and instruments within and across countries and along migration routes.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical and operational leadership for the regional and inter-regional operationalisation of IOM’s RteBA, in line with its institutional framework, and in coordination with relevant COs, Regional Offices (ROs), HQ divisions and global RteBA coordination structures; lead the development and implementation of multi-country, multi-partner operational plans for relevant routes; and ensure coherence with IOM’s institutional priorities, relevant regional strategies, and country-level operational realities.
2. Oversee the region’s RteBA Flexible Funding Mechanism allocation and other assigned RteBA projects, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery against approved results frameworks, workplans, budgets, indicators and donor requirements; monitor overall implementation and take or recommend corrective action to address delivery, quality and resource issues.
3. Serve as the RO’s RteBA focal point and lead the region’s engagement and participation in the global RteBA Task Force and, together with specific RTSs, its workstreams. Ensure that regional needs and priorities are reflected in global instruments, deliver agreed regional inputs on schedule, and lead the testing of operational guidance in the region.
4. In close coordination with RPLOs and relevant COs, lead government engagement on the RteBA to anchor route-based action in the priorities of States along relevant migration routes and reflect those priorities in regional cooperation processes. Provide route-level analysis, strategic advice and positioning to regional consultative processes, cross-regional discussions, and intergovernmental dialogues.
5. Support the Policy and Liaison Unit in providing substantive and coordination support to the Regional United Nations Network on Migration (RUNNM), including developing activities, promoting complementarity, and facilitating information exchange among regional RUNNM structures, the UNNM at the global level, IOM’s internal route-based coordination arrangements, and other relevant regional and inter-regional mechanisms.
6. In coordination with the Regional Director and Deputy Regional Director, lead the development and maintenance of strategic partnerships in support of the RteBA with United Nations (UN) agencies, international and national Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), civil society, migrant- and community-led organisations, academia, the private sector and other relevant actors. Provide substantive advice on partnership opportunities and approaches in support of regional RteBA priorities.
7. In close coordination with RPDOs and relevant RTSs, lead the coordination of coherent and integrated RteBA programming across global, regional and country levels, ensuring alignment of programme concepts, proposals and funding approaches through effective coordination with relevant technical and operational teams. Participate in the development of funding strategies and resource mobilisation initiatives, including through engagement with donors and strategic partners, and provide substantive inputs on regional funding priorities and opportunities.
8. In coordination with the relevant RTSs and the RPLOs, lead the translation of route-level analysis and operational experience into regional and inter-regional policy advice, practical guidance, capacity building priorities and coordinated support for Member States, UN Country Teams (UNCT) and country networks.
9. Lead efforts to strengthen institutional capacity and organisational learning for route-based programming by supporting the development, adaptation and institutionalisation of RteBA tools, guidance, methodologies, standard operating procedures, knowledge products and good practices within IOM.
10. Establish and maintain route-level coordination mechanisms among IOM COs and, where relevant, other ROs along migration routes; convene regular route coordination meetings; provide route-level guidance; and oversee the implementation of agreed multi-country, multi-partner operational plans.
11. In coordination with RPDOs and Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officers (RPMEOs), coordinate the development and dissemination of route-level evidence, knowledge management products, diagnostic assessments, lessons learned and analytical outputs to support a shared understanding of priority migration routes, and formulate recommendations to inform regional programming and decision-making.
12. Contribute to institutional learning, results-based monitoring, donor engagement and strategic decision-making by leading the consolidation and communication of regional and route-level insights and providing substantive recommendations to inform programme priorities, implementation and policy development.
13. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer, Cultural Orientation for Switchboard, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded program. Switchboard is a one-stop resource hub for refugee service providers in the United States. Switchboard provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:UsersTigestCoAppDataLocalMicrosoftOlkAttachmentsooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdbwww.SwitchboardTA.org).

Settle In is Switchboard's digital information service for newcomers taking the knowledge and resources Switchboard offers to service providers and adapting and delivering it directly to newcomers**,** in multiple languages, through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org/.

Cultural orientation is a core service in refugee resettlement in the United States, helping newcomers build the knowledge and skills to navigate life in their new communities. The Training Officer, Cultural Orientation, leads the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives for these programs. This includes training and technical assistance (TTA) to service providers, helping them build strong cultural orientation programs and apply best practices when working with newcomers. This staff member is responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective cultural orientation resources such as curricula, training materials, and learning tools, and facilitating learning experiences that improve outcomes for newcomer children, adults, and families. This role requires hands-on experience working directly with clients, subject matter experts, and partners, along with prior experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Design and deliver versatile cultural orientation training to service providers and cultural orientation delivery staff.
- Provide responsive and cross-disciplinary technical assistance to refugee service providers in response to cultural orientation TTAs, adapting content to meet varied organizational needs and learning styles.
- In collaboration with colleagues across teams, develop written and multimedia learning resources (e.g., toolkits, videos, podcasts) that reflect trauma-informed, client-centered, and strength-based approaches.
- Adapt materials for different literacy levels, languages, and cultural contexts
- Integrate feedback from internal and external reviewers to continuously improve training and resource contents and delivery methods.
- Facilitate communities of practice and peer learning groups to promote knowledge exchange and cross-training across service areas.

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage internal and external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

- Other duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Required:**

- Bachelor's degree required, preferably in a related field such as Education, International Development, Social Work, Public Administration, Cross-Cultural Studies, Migration/Refugee Studies, or a related social science (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience in supporting newcomers' access and gaining self-sufficiency for services and resources i.e. financial, medical, social, vocational etc.

**Preferred:**

- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Strong understanding of cultural orientation frameworks, refugee/newcomer integration principles, and adult learning principles
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.
- Strong attention to detail
